Faith is stronger than mountains. The Lord does not say that faith will move you a mountain for show, but that nothing is impossible to those who believe; and the thing that is most impossible, the conversion of a hard heart, is moved by prayer.
St Augustine (in substance)

Those who love the truth find truth where they find God, because God is truth. Let us not be among those who love the sound of wonders more than the truth; whoever loves the truth does not fear to be corrected.
magis: Catechism 675

Before Christ's second coming the Church must pass through a final trial that will shake the faith of many believers; the deception of evil and the mystery of iniquity will be unmasked, and only the truth will stand.
Catechism 2053

In the Gospel Jesus tells the young man who asks what to do: if you would be perfect, go, sell what you possess and give to the poor, and come, follow me; the commandments are the beginning of the way.
Catechism 2610-2611
Jesus calls us to pray with faith: whatever you ask in prayer, believe that you have received it; prayer of faith is not only words but a disposing of the heart to the will of the Father.
saints: Fourth Saturday of Kaitha. Saint Ignatius of Loyola (about 1491–1556), priest, founder of the Society of Jesus (the Jesuits). In the Latin calendar, his memorial.
Sunday 1 August, the Fifth Sunday of Kaitha (verify locally).

25–31 July: the fourth week of the Season of Kaitha. Sun 25: Fourth Sunday of Kaitha (St James the Apostle gives way to the Sunday; World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly). Mon 26: Sts Joachim and Anne, the parents of the Blessed Virgin Mary. Wed 28: St Alphonsa, the first woman of Indian origin to be canonised, an important feast. Thu 29: St Martha. Fri 30: Fourth Friday of Kaitha. Sat 31: St Ignatius of Loyola. In the Latin calendar the same days keep Sts Joachim and Anne (26), St Alphonsa (28, a memorial in India), Sts Martha, Mary and Lazarus (29) and St Ignatius (31). Looking ahead: the month of August and the later weeks of Kaitha.
2027-07-31.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, you called Ignatius from the battlefield to the service of your kingdom, and taught him to find you in all things. Teach us to do everything for your glory: our work and our rest, our eating and our prayer. Give us the courage to count the cost and to put you before everything, and the faith to ask you for great things. Keep us from deception, and give us a love of the truth that tests every spirit and holds to what is good. Bless the Jesuits and all who teach in the schools and colleges of our land. Take, Lord, and receive our liberty, our memory, our understanding and our will; give us only your love and your grace, and we shall be rich enough. Amen.
altar: At the Holy Qurbana the bread and the wine are placed before God, and so is our whole day. We offer them for his glory, and he gives himself back to us as food. Ignatius sat before the altar with his sword laid down; so we sit before it with our worries, our work and our plans, and say: Take, Lord, and receive.

quick: Dukhrana (remembrance) of Mar Thoma, the Apostle Thomas, our father in faith: an important feast and a day of obligation; the last day of the Season of the Apostles.
John: a week after Easter Jesus comes again for Thomas, shows his wounds, and Thomas confesses, “My Lord and my God!”; blessed are those who have not seen and believe.

Ephesians: the Church is built on the foundation of the apostles, with Christ as the cornerstone; Genesis and Proverbs: the garden in the east, the tree of life, and the path of the righteous like the light of dawn.
The Seventh Saturday: Paul calls married people to peace and fidelity; Jesus recalls God's plan for marriage from the beginning.
2027-07-03.action: At the elevation in the Qurbana, say in your heart, “My Lord and my God,” and tell one young person how the faith came to your family.
2027-07-03.question: If I could ask the risen Lord for one sign, what would it be, and am I ready to say “My Lord and my God” even without it?
catechism: Thomas and the doubt of the disciples.
Marriage from the beginning; Jesus and Moses' permission.
The believing spouse in a marriage with a non-believer.
The marriage bond and the Church's care.
kidsaint: St Thomas the Apostle

Thomas was one of Jesus' twelve friends. He was brave: when Jesus was going to a dangerous place, Thomas said, ‘Let us also go!’ He asked honest questions, too. When Jesus rose from the dead, Thomas was not there, and he said, ‘I will believe when I see.’ Jesus came back for him, and Thomas said, ‘My Lord and my God!’ After that Thomas went far away. According to tradition he came by boat to Kerala, told people about Jesus, baptised them and started churches, and he died at Mylapore near Chennai. Lesson: ask your questions, be brave, and tell others about Jesus, as Thomas did!
2027-07-03.special: Dukhrana of St Thomas the Apostle: an important feast and a day of obligation; the last day of the Season of the Apostles. Kaitha begins tomorrow.
term: Dukhrana

A Syriac word meaning remembrance or memorial. In the East Syriac tradition, 3 July is the Dukhrana of St Thomas, the day on which his relics are remembered as brought to Edessa. In the Syro-Malabar Church it is the great feast of our father in faith. Malayalam: ദുക്റാന.

family.explain: Thomas was one of Jesus' friends. After Jesus rose from the dead, Thomas was not in the room when Jesus came, and the others told him, ‘We have seen the Lord!’ Thomas said, ‘I will believe only when I see.’ Eight days later Jesus came again and said to Thomas, ‘Peace be with you. Look at my hands.’ Thomas said, ‘My Lord and my God!’ And Jesus said that people who believe without seeing are blessed: that means us! Our Church says that Thomas came to Kerala by boat and told our people about Jesus, so Thomas is our father in faith.
family.intention: We thank God for the faith of our grandparents and for every priest, sister and teacher who handed it on, and we pray for all Christians of India.
family.ask: Ask: “Who first told us about Jesus in our family, and how can we thank them?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Palayoor (a story told to illustrate the reading) a boy of ten once asked his grandmother after the Dukhrana Qurbana, ‘Ammachi, did Mar Thoma really come here? How do you know?’ The old woman smiled. ‘I was not there, mon, and neither was my mother. But my mother's mother told my mother, and my mother told me, and I have told you. In our family every grandmother has said, Mar Thoma brought us the faith. That is how we know: someone told someone, and each one loved enough to pass it on.’ The boy thought for a while and said, ‘So it is like Thomas and the Lord. He did not see Mar Thoma, but he believes.’ The grandmother laughed and touched his head. ‘Blessed are those who have not seen, my child, and yet have believed.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you came through closed doors and said “Peace” to your disciples and to Thomas. Gather us in your name and give us the faith of Thomas. Amen.
share: Let us also go, that we may die with him (John 11:16). Where is Jesus calling me to go, even though it is hard?
How can we know the way? (John 14:5). What question about my faith do I carry, and have I brought it to the Lord?
Put your finger here and see my hands (John 20:27). How have I seen the Lord's wounds in the poor and the suffering?
My Lord and my God! (John 20:28). Can I say this today from my heart, and what would change if I meant it?
pm.resp: My Lord and my God!
interc: For the Church in India, founded on the faith of Saint Thomas, that she may remain faithful and be a sign of Christ in every land.
For the Syro-Malabar Church and her missions in India and across the world.
For all Christians who share the heritage of Saint Thomas, the Orthodox, Mar Thoma and Malankara Churches, that we may grow in unity and peace.
For those who doubt and for those who are searching for the truth, that they may find Christ.
For families, that they may be places where faith is handed on and where the peace of Christ is lived.
pm.close: Father, you gave the Church of India the apostle Thomas as father in faith. Through his prayers keep us on the Way, make us glad witnesses of your Son, and bring us to the joy of those who believe without seeing. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The Feast of the Twelve Apostles opens the Season of Kaitha: the apostles sowed the Gospel, and the Church now contemplates its growth and harvest.
Elijah rebuilds the altar with twelve stones and the fire of the Lord falls; the people say, “The Lord indeed is God.”
The apostles do many signs; an angel opens the prison and sends them back to teach in the Temple. Paul: Christ is not divided; be united in the same mind.
Jesus: take the lowest place at the banquet, and invite those who cannot repay you.
2027-07-04.action: Learn the names of the Twelve this week and pray them at evening prayer; at the next parish meal, take the last seat.
2027-07-04.question: Where am I looking for the seat of honour, and where is the Lord asking me to sit lower?
kidsaint: The Twelve Apostles

Jesus had twelve special friends, called apostles: Peter, Andrew, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, Matthew, James, Thaddaeus, Simon, and Judas, who was later replaced by Matthias. They were fishermen, a tax collector and ordinary working people. Jesus asked them to be with him and then to go and tell everyone about God. They did not always understand, and once they even argued about who was the greatest! But Jesus taught them to serve, and the Holy Spirit made them brave. Lesson: you do not have to be perfect to be Jesus' friend. Say yes, stay close to him, and then go and tell others!
2027-07-04.special: First Sunday of Kaitha and Feast of the Twelve Apostles: the season of Kaitha (summer) begins.
term: Šliha (Apostle)

The Syriac word for an apostle means one who is sent. Our Malayalam word ശ്ലീഹാ comes from it. The Twelve were first called to be with Jesus and then sent out. The season that has just ended is called the Season of the Apostles (ശ്ലീഹാക്കാലം). Kaitha (Qaita), the season that begins today, means summer.

family.explain: Jesus once saw people at a dinner hurrying to take the best seats. He said: when you are invited, sit in the last place; then the host may say, ‘Friend, come up higher!’ He also said: when you have a feast, invite people who have nothing and cannot give you anything back, and God will bless you. Today the Church remembers Jesus' twelve special friends, the apostles. They learned to serve and not to push for the best place. When we do small things for others, we are like the apostles.
family.intention: We pray for our parish, our priests, and all who help to prepare the feast, and for people who go hungry or who sit alone.
family.ask: Ask: “Who can we invite to share a meal this month, someone who cannot invite us back?”

illus: An illustration

In a hill parish in Idukki (a story told to illustrate the reading) the feast of the church was always a big meal after the Qurbana. The front benches were kept for the guests of honour, and the old catechist Mathai, who had taught three generations, always came late from his field and stood at the back. One year the new priest, noticing him, stopped in the middle of the announcements. ‘Mathai chettan, there is a seat here.’ Mathai smiled and said, ‘Achen, I am comfortable at the back.’ The priest said, ‘Then let us all move to the back.’ And the whole church laughed and made room, and the priest sat down on the last bench himself. That year, for the first time, the feast meal was served first to the old people and the children and to the families that had no money to give, and the guests of honour waited and were served last, and nobody remembered the seating afterwards. They remembered how happy the whole parish was.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you called the Twelve to be with you and to be sent. Gather us now as your friends, and send us out again with your Spirit. Amen.
share: Elijah took twelve stones (1 Kings 18:31). What stones, what people and what truths is my life built on?
Go, stand in the temple and tell the people the whole message (Acts 5:20). Do I tell only the welcome parts of the Gospel, or the whole?
Has Christ been divided? (1 Corinthians 1:13). Where in my family or parish do I take sides, and what would it take to be one?
Go and sit down at the lowest place (Luke 14:10). Where am I choosing the places of honour?
pm.resp: Lord, make us one in you.
interc: For the Pope, our Major Archbishop, our bishops and all the successors of the apostles, that they may be servants of unity.
For our parishes, that they may be places where the lowest place is loved and the poor are first at the table.
For the unity of all Christians, especially with the Churches that share the heritage of Saint Thomas.
For farmers and for those who work in the fields in this monsoon season, and for a good harvest.
For young people who are being called by Jesus, that they may answer.
pm.close: Father, you built your Church on the foundation of the apostles. As we begin this season of growth and harvest, keep us united in mind and purpose, humble in heart, and generous to the poor, so that we may bring forth fruit that lasts. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Deuteronomy: because the Lord loved your ancestors he chose their descendants; acknowledge today that the Lord is God.
Isaiah: the Branch of the Lord, the holy remnant, and a canopy as a shade by day and a shelter from storm and rain.
Paul: our competence is from God; the new covenant is of the Spirit, who gives life; we act with boldness.
Luke: the father runs to the returning son, and goes out again to plead with the elder one.
2027-07-11.action: Pray each evening this week for one person who has gone away from the faith or from the family, and say to someone at home: ‘I am glad you are here.’
2027-07-11.question: Am I the younger son who needs to return, or the elder who will not come in?
catechism: The covenants and the Jewish people.
Pardon in the sacrament of Penance.
kidsaint: St Euphrasia of Eluvathingal

A girl called Rosa was born in 1877 at Kattoor near Thrissur in Kerala. As a young woman she joined the Carmelite sisters who followed Father Chavara, and she took the name Euphrasia. She prayed for hours before Jesus in the tabernacle, especially for people who had gone far from God, so that they might come home like the son in today's Gospel. She died in 1952, and Pope Francis declared her a saint in 2014, together with St Chavara. Lesson: you can bring someone home to God by praying for them every day.
2027-07-11.special: Second Sunday of Kaitha: the father who runs to meet his lost son.
term: Mar

A Syriac word meaning ‘my lord’, used as a title of honour for saints and bishops in the Syriac tradition: Mar Thoma, Mar Yakob, Mar Mari, Mar Addai. In the calendar of Kaitha it appears again and again, because this season remembers the saints of the East Syriac Church. Malayalam: മാർ.

family.explain: A boy took his father's money and went far away and spent it all. When he was hungry he decided to go home. Before he even reached the door, his father saw him from far off and ran to meet him and hugged him! The father gave him new clothes and made a big feast. Our heavenly Father is just like that. However far we go, he is watching the road, and he is always glad to see us come home.
family.intention: We pray for people who are far from home, for children who are away at school or work, and for those who have no family.
family.ask: Ask: “When did someone welcome us back after we did something wrong, and how did it feel?”

illus: An illustration

In a village near Changanassery (a story told to illustrate the reading) an old father kept the front-gate lamp lit every night for ten years, though his younger son had gone to the Gulf and stopped writing. His elder son thought it a waste of oil and said so. ‘He will come back when he is ready,’ said the old man, ‘and I want him to see the light.’ One monsoon evening a thin man in a wet shirt stood at the gate and did not dare to come in. The old man was on the road before the dogs had barked. The elder brother stood at the veranda and could not move. Later that night the old man said to him, ‘Come and sit with us. The house is full tonight, and you are the one who kept it standing.’ The elder son sat down, and the lamp was left lit.

pm.open: Heavenly Father, who run to meet us on the road, gather us in your house, and let us hear your voice saying: you are my son, my daughter. Amen.
share: Because he loved your ancestors, he chose their descendants after them (Deuteronomy 4:37). How has God's love been shown to my family before I was born?
A canopy, a shade by day from the heat, and a refuge from the storm and rain (Isaiah 4:6). Where in my life do I need such a shelter today?
The Spirit gives life (2 Corinthians 3:6). Where am I living by the letter only?
While he was still far off, his father saw him (Luke 15:20). What would I say if I went home to the Father today?
pm.resp: Father, we have sinned; receive us.
interc: For the Church in the season of Kaitha, that she may be a canopy of mercy for all who are in the heat and the storm.
For those who have left the faith or the family, that they may find the way home.
For all who feel unworthy to be called sons and daughters, that they may hear the Father's welcome.
For priests and confessors, that they may be like the father who runs to meet the penitent.
For those of us who have stayed at home, that we may share the joy of the Father.
pm.close: Father, you have made us for yourself. Bring us home, bring home those we love, and seat us all at your table, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: James: consider trials as joy, for faith tested produces endurance; ask God for wisdom in faith.
Mark: the fruitless fig tree, faith that moves mountains, and the condition of forgiveness.

St Kuriakose and St Julitta: a mother and her three-year-old son confess Christ at Tarsus (about 304, according to the ancient Acts). Daniel, Stephen, Hebrews and Matthew 10 show the courage of witness.
2027-07-15.action: Forgive one person before your next prayer, and answer one question about your faith simply and kindly.
2027-07-15.question: Would I say, “I am a Christian”, in my own words and in my own place?

family.explain: Long ago there was a mother called Julitta and her little boy Kuriakose, who was only three. Soldiers who did not love Jesus asked them to say they did not believe in him. The mother said she believed in Jesus, and the little boy said: “I am a Christian too.” They were not afraid, because Jesus had told his friends: “Do not be afraid; you are of more value than many sparrows.” God took them to heaven as martyrs. Today we can also say proudly, in kind words, that we love Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for children who are teased because of their faith, for families who are afraid, and for all Christians who suffer for the name of Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “When did we last say sorry or forgive someone before we prayed? What can we do tonight?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Kothamangalam (a story told to illustrate the reading) a three-year-old boy named Kuriakose was carried to the church on the feast of his patron. In the bus a stranger asked him, ‘What is your name?’ and he answered at the top of his voice, ‘Kuriakose! Mar Kuriakose's boy!’ The whole bus laughed, and his mother blushed. Twenty-five years later Kuriakose was a nurse in a hospital in a distant city, where many colleagues asked him questions about his faith. He answered the same way: simply, kindly, without fear and without a quarrel. When a young colleague asked how he could be so sure, he said, ‘I learned it before I could count. Mar Kuriakose was three years old; I only had to be three once.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you promised that you would acknowledge before the Father those who acknowledge you before people. Gather us now in this prayer, and give us the courage of Saint Julitta and her little son. Amen.
share: Consider it nothing but joy whenever you face trials (James 1:2). Which trial of mine could become a school of endurance?
If any of you is lacking in wisdom, ask God (James 1:5). What decision am I carrying alone?
Have faith in God (Mark 11:22). What mountain do I hold in my heart that I have stopped asking God to move?
Forgive, if you have anything against anyone (Mark 11:25). Whom must I forgive before I can pray in peace?
pm.resp: Lord, give us a faith that does not fear.
interc: For children and young people who are teased or pressed because of their faith, that they may answer with simple courage.
For Christians in places where the faith is dangerous, that the Spirit may speak in them in the hour of trial.
For mothers and fathers who hand on the faith, that their witness may remain in their children.
For all who are tried by sickness, loss or doubt, that they may ask God for wisdom and receive it.
For ourselves, that we may forgive from the heart and speak of Jesus plainly and kindly.
pm.close: Father, you gave your martyrs a strength beyond their years and their power. Make us faithful in small things and in great, and bring us to the city built by you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Deuteronomy: the Lord who brought Israel out of slavery gives the Ten Words; keep the Sabbath and honour your parents.
Isaiah: the vineyard of the Lord yields wild grapes; he expected justice and heard a cry.
Paul: godly grief produces a repentance that leads to salvation; worldly grief produces death.
John: Jesus gives sight to a man born blind, and the man worships the Son of Man.
2027-07-18.action: Keep this Sunday as the Lord's Day: go to the Holy Qurbana, rest, and give time to your family; then make one act of reparation to someone you have wronged.
2027-07-18.question: What fruit does the Lord find in my life, and for what do I need to turn back to him?
catechism: The Ten Words in the setting of the Exodus.
kidsaint: St Euphrasia of Kerala

Rosa Eluvathingal was born in 1877 in Kattoor, near Thrissur, in Kerala. Even as a girl she loved to pray and wanted to belong to God. She became a sister of the Congregation of the Mother of Carmel, and was later called Mother Eupraseia. She spent long hours before the Blessed Sacrament, and she cared for the sick and the poor with a happy heart. People called her the praying mother. Pope Francis declared her a saint on 23 November 2014, together with St Kuriakose Elias Chavara. When you pray, remember that a child from Kerala became a saint by praying and by loving.
2027-07-18.special: Third Sunday of Kaitha. In the Latin calendar, the Sixteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time.
term: Decalogue

Greek for “ten words”. The Ten Commandments are the first words of the covenant, given by God to Israel at Sinai after he brought them out of slavery. They are found in Exodus 20 and Deuteronomy 5. Jesus said that they are summed up in love of God and love of neighbour.

family.explain: One day Jesus saw a man who had been blind from the day he was born. Jesus made a little mud and put it on the man's eyes, and said, “Go and wash in the pool of Siloam.” The man went, and washed, and he could see! He saw the sky and the faces of his friends for the first time. Later Jesus met him again and asked, “Do you believe?” And the man said, “Lord, I believe.” Jesus is the light of the world. He helps us to see how to love God and our neighbour.
family.intention: We pray for those who cannot see, for the ones who are sick, and for people who are lost, that Jesus may be their light.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing that Jesus has helped us see more clearly this week?”

illus: An illustration

At an eye camp organised by a parish near Muvattupuzha (a story told to illustrate the reading) an old farmer who had not seen the faces of his grandchildren for three years had both his cataracts removed. When the bandages came off, the nurse held up a small crucifix and asked, ‘What do you see?’ He said nothing for a moment, and then he whispered, ‘Is that you, Mariyamma?’ to his wife of fifty years, whom he had not seen clearly in all that time. At the church the next Sunday the vicar asked him to say a few words. ‘In the dark years I thought God had forgotten me,’ he said. ‘Now I see that all that time someone sent a doctor, a driver and a daughter-in-law who held my hand. The doctor opened my eyes last week, but the real seeing began long ago.’ Then he said, louder, the words of the man in the Gospel: ‘Lord, I believe.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the world, you found the man who had been cast out and you opened his eyes. Gather us in your light and open our eyes to see you in the Scriptures, in the Qurbana and in our neighbour. Amen.
share: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt (Deuteronomy 5:6). From what has God already rescued me?
He expected it to yield grapes, but it yielded wild grapes (Isaiah 5:2). What fruit does God look for in me, and what have I given him?
Godly grief produces a repentance that leads to salvation (2 Corinthians 7:10). What am I sorry for, and is my sorrow turning me to God?
Do you believe in the Son of Man? (John 9:35). What does “Lord, I believe” mean for my life this week?
pm.resp: Lord, I believe; help my unbelief.
interc: For the Church, that she may keep the commandments in love and bear the fruit of justice and mercy in the world.
For all who are tempted to despair after failure, that they may turn to the Lord with godly grief and find mercy.
For the blind and all who have lost sight, and for those who are blind to the needs of others, that Christ may open their eyes.
For our parents and grandparents, that they may be honoured and cared for in their old age.
For ourselves, that on the Lord's Day we may rest, pray and give thanks.
pm.close: Father, you give us your law as a gift and your Son as the light. Keep us in your vineyard, make us fruitful, and open our eyes to see you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Deuteronomy: the Ten Words spoken out of the fire; honour your father and mother, that it may go well with you.
Isaiah: the people did not turn to him who struck them; the fire of wickedness; Manasseh devoured Ephraim.
Paul: do not compare yourselves with others; boast only in the Lord.
Mark: the tradition of the elders must not void the commandment of God; the example of Corban and the care of parents.
2027-07-25.action: Spend time with an elderly person in your family this week, and do one concrete thing for them.
2027-07-25.question: Is there any gift or custom of mine that lets me escape what God plainly asks of me?
kidsaint: St Monica

Saint Monica lived in North Africa about sixteen hundred years ago. She loved her son Augustine very much, and when he went far from God she prayed and cried for him for many years. God heard her. Augustine became a great saint and a bishop, and he wrote that he owed much to his mother's tears. Lesson: love and honour your parents and grandparents, and pray for them every day.
2027-07-25.special: Fourth Sunday of Kaitha. World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly.
term: Corban (Qorban)

A Hebrew word for a gift dedicated to God (Mark 7:11). It comes from a root meaning to draw near, which is also the root of the Syriac word Qurbana, the offering we call the Holy Qurbana. A gift is truly Corban only when it does not take away what God commands us to give to others.

family.explain: Jesus said that some people honoured God with words, but their hearts were far away. God's fourth commandment says: honour your father and your mother. Some people said, ‘I have given my money to God, so I cannot help my parents.’ Jesus said that was wrong. To love God is also to look after the old people in our home. Grandfathers and grandmothers are God's special gifts to us.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and for every old person who is lonely.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing we can do for an old person this week: a visit, a call, a drawing, a prayer?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in the hills of Idukki (a story told to illustrate the reading) a family gave a large sum for the new bell tower, and their name was cut into the stone. The vicar, who visited homes on Saturdays, found the grandmother of that family in a back room, with a single plate and no one to talk to; the son was busy with the building committee. He said nothing at first. At the dedication he blessed the tower, and then asked the family to bring grandmother to the front row. ‘The bell calls us to God,’ he said quietly, ‘but I think this lady is the first bell of your house.’ The son wept. From that day the old woman sat at the family table every evening. The vicar often said afterwards that he had only repeated Jesus' words about Corban.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you showed us that the word of God must never be made void by our traditions. Gather us now, and teach us to honour our fathers and mothers and to keep our hearts clean. Amen.
share: Honor your father and your mother (Deuteronomy 5:16). How do I honour my parents or grandparents, living or dead?
This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me (Mark 7:6). Where is my prayer only on the lips?
The people did not turn to him who struck them (Isaiah 9:13). What do I need to turn back to the Lord about?
Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord (2 Corinthians 10:17). Of what am I proud, and is it a gift?
pm.resp: Lord, let your word never be made void in us.
interc: For the Church, that her traditions may always serve the commandments of God and the Gospel.
For grandparents and the elderly, that they may be honoured, cared for and never left alone.
For families divided by quarrels over land, money or old hurts, that they may find peace.
For those who give to the Church and the poor, that their giving may come from a loving heart.
For parents and children of our parish, that they may honour one another in love.
pm.close: Father of every family, you gave us your Son to be born among a family and to be honoured by a mother. Bless the elderly among us and make us a household that keeps your commandment. Amen.

quick: Paul: because of God's mercy we do not lose heart; we use no cunning and do not falsify God's word, but state the truth openly.
Paul: we proclaim not ourselves but Jesus Christ as Lord; God has shone in our hearts the light of his glory in the face of Christ.
Jesus: woe to the teachers who lock people out of the kingdom and play clever games with oaths; the altar, the sanctuary and heaven all belong to God.
2027-07-01.action: Keep one promise you have delayed, and for a day let every word you say be one you would say in God's presence.
2027-07-01.question: Is my Yes a Yes, or do I keep a loophole ready?

family.read: Read together: Matthew 23:16–22 (the question about the gold and the temple).
family.explain: Some teachers in Jesus' time said clever things about promises: if you swear by this, it does not count; if you swear by that, it counts. Jesus said: God hears every word, so tell the truth every time. When we say Yes, we should mean Yes, and when we say No, we should mean No. Paul tells us that Jesus is the light of the world: the light shines out of the face of Jesus, and we can carry a little of that light in our words.
family.intention: We pray for teachers, priests and catechists, that they may speak the truth with love, and for everyone who finds it hard to keep a promise.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one promise our family made and has not yet kept?”

illus: An illustration

In a small town near Kottayam (a story told to illustrate the reading) a shopkeeper named Varkey had a board hanging above his weighing scale. It said: ‘My word is my weight.’ A customer once teased him: ‘Everyone says that, Chettan. Why don't you swear on the scale, then?’ Varkey smiled. ‘If I need to swear, I have already weighed wrongly.’ He kept a small picture of the Sacred Heart beside the scale and, each morning before opening, touched the glass of the picture and said, ‘Let me weigh as You see.’ When he died, the whole market closed for the funeral, and the scale was left in the shop window with the board still above it.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the world, you see the heart behind every word. Gather us now, and let the truth be spoken among us in love. Amen.
share: We do not lose heart (2 Corinthians 4:1). What discourages me in my service of the Lord, and where do I find strength?
We refuse to practice cunning (2 Corinthians 4:2). In what small ways do I still bend the truth to my advantage?
We proclaim Jesus Christ as Lord (2 Corinthians 4:5). When people look at my life, whom do they see first?
Which is greater, the gift or the altar that makes the gift sacred? (Matthew 23:19). Do I treat what is holy with the reverence it deserves?
pm.resp: Lord, let our Yes be Yes.
interc: For priests, catechists and all who preach the Word, that they may proclaim Christ and not themselves.
For judges, witnesses and officials who take oaths, that truth may guide every word.
For those who have lost heart in the Lord's service, that his mercy may renew them.
For people who feel locked out of the Church by harsh words, that they may find an open door.
For ourselves, that we may be honest in speech and faithful in promises.
pm.close: Father, you made light shine out of darkness and have shown us your glory in the face of your Son. Keep our hearts open to the truth, make our word trustworthy, and let us be a door to your kingdom for others. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus appoints seventy others and sends them ahead of him in pairs: the harvest is plentiful, the labourers few.
Isaiah: God will open rivers in the wilderness for the poor and the thirsty. Paul: God has brought to Israel a Saviour, Jesus, as he promised.
Paul: all things work together for good for those who love God; nothing can separate us from the love of Christ.
Jesus: love him above all, take up the cross, and welcome others; even a cup of cold water given in his name will have its reward.
2027-07-02.action: Pray every day this week for more labourers for the harvest, and give a glass of water and a kind word to someone who does not expect it.
2027-07-02.question: Who has welcomed me in the name of Christ, and whom can I welcome today?

family.explain: Jesus once sent seventy of his friends to the towns and villages where he wanted to go. They went in twos, and they said, ‘Peace to this house!’ They told people that God's kingdom was near. Jesus also said that even a glass of cold water given in his name will have a reward. In our Church, two of those friends are special: Mar Addai and Mar Mari, because the prayer of our Holy Qurbana is called by their names.
family.intention: We pray for priests, sisters, brothers and all missionaries, and for people who have no one to welcome them.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom can we welcome with a glass of water and a smile this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a village in Kuttanad (a story told to illustrate the reading) a retired schoolteacher named Annamma kept a clay pot of cool water and a steel tumbler on a stool at her gate. Walkers on the dusty road stopped to drink, and she always said ‘God bless you’. One July a tired young man with a bag stopped there. He had been told that no one in the village would rent a room to a stranger. Annamma looked at him and said, ‘You will eat first.’ She gave him rice and fish curry, and a neighbour's room for the night. Many years later the young man, now a priest in a distant mission, wrote to her: ‘You were the first church I met in Kuttanad.’ She kept the letter next to her rosary until she died.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you sent your disciples in pairs to proclaim your peace. Gather us now, and send us out again with the same peace. Amen.
share: The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few (Luke 10:2). What is the Lord asking of me for his harvest?
I will open rivers on the bare heights (Isaiah 41:18). Where in my life or in my parish is the ground dry, and what can I bring?
If God is for us, who is against us? (Romans 8:31). What fear keeps me from being sent?
Whoever welcomes you welcomes me (Matthew 10:40). Whom did Christ send to welcome me?
pm.resp: Lord of the harvest, send us out in your peace.
interc: For the Church, that every baptised person may take part in the mission of Christ.
For priests, religious and missionaries, that they may not lose heart in their work.
For those who are thirsty in body or in spirit, that they may find springs of living water.
For the persecuted and the poor, that nothing may separate them from the love of Christ.
For our families, that they may be open, welcoming homes.
pm.close: Father, you gave your Son a heart open to every thirst, and you sent disciples to every town. Make us joyful messengers of peace, generous in welcome and sure of your love, until we come to the springs of the water of life. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul rebukes Corinth: they come together, but the rich eat first and the poor are humiliated; it is not really the Lord's supper.
Paul gives the oldest account of the Eucharist: this is my body for you; do this in memory of me; as often as you eat you proclaim the Lord's death.
Jesus: the parable of the two sons; the one who said No and then went did the Father's will.
Not everyone who says “Lord, Lord” enters the kingdom, but the one who does the Father's will.
2027-07-05.action: Make peace with someone before the next Qurbana, and do today the one task you have said Later to.
2027-07-05.question: Is my Yes to the Lord a Yes of words, or a Yes of hands?

family.explain: A father asked his two sons to go and work in the vineyard. One son said, ‘I will not!’ but later he was sorry and went. The other son said, ‘Yes, sir!’ but did not go. Jesus asked: which son did what his father wanted? The one who went. A Yes with no work is just words. Saint Paul also teaches that when we come to Holy Qurbana, we must share with others and not leave anyone hungry.
family.intention: We pray for children and families who go hungry, and for ourselves, that we may say a true Yes to God.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one job at home that we said Later to, and can we do it together today?”

illus: An illustration

In a village in Pathanamthitta (a story told to illustrate the reading) a farmer named Kuruvila had two sons. One day in the monsoon he asked both to help him prepare the nursery for the paddy seedlings. The elder, Binu, said, ‘Appa, it is pouring. I will not go.’ The younger, Biju, said, ‘Yes, Appa, I am coming’, and went back to his phone. An hour later Binu took the umbrella and a mamoty and went to the field without a word. By evening the whole nursery was ready. When Kuruvila came home, he found Biju on the veranda with a plate of rice. Biju said, ‘Appa, I was just coming.’ Kuruvila looked at the muddy boots at the door and said quietly, ‘Binu said no, and he worked. You said yes, and your hands were clean.’ After supper Biju took the empty plate to the kitchen and put on his boots. The next morning he was in the field before the others.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you broke bread for us and said, “Do this in remembrance of me.” Gather us as one body, and teach us to say a Yes that works. Amen.
share: It is not really to eat the Lord's supper (1 Corinthians 11:20). Where in my parish or family do we divide the table?
Do you show contempt for the church of God and humiliate those who have nothing? (1 Corinthians 11:22). Whom do I overlook?
Did the will of his father (Matthew 21:31). Where have I said Yes and not done it, or No and later changed?
Go and work in the vineyard today (Matthew 21:28). What is the Father asking me to do today?
pm.resp: Lord, let our Yes be true.
interc: For our parishes, that the Holy Qurbana may be a sign of unity between rich and poor.
For all who go hungry, and for those who feed them.
For those who have said No to God and are being called back, that they may change their minds and return.
For farmers working in the monsoon fields, that their labour may bear fruit.
For ourselves, that we may do the Father's will and not only speak of it.
pm.close: Father, your Son gave himself for us in the Body and Blood, and teaches us to do your will. Make us one at your table, generous to the poor, and faithful to our word, until we sit at the banquet of your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: be infants in evil but adult in thinking; in worship let the word be understood, so that the outsider says, “God is really among you.”
Luke: the nobleman gives ten servants a pound each; two trade and are praised; the third buries his, out of fear.
The lesson: God's gifts are given to be used; the picture of God as harsh makes us idle.
Saint Maria Goretti, aged eleven, refused to sin, forgave her attacker and died on 6 July 1902; canonised in 1950.
2027-07-06.action: Write down one gift you have and one way to use it for others this month; at the Qurbana notice what a stranger would see.
2027-07-06.question: Have I buried a gift out of fear, and what picture of God lies behind it?

family.explain: A rich man went on a long journey. Before he left, he gave his servants money and said, ‘Use this until I come back.’ When he returned, two servants had used the money well. One servant had hidden it in a cloth because he was afraid. The master was pleased with the two who had worked, because each had been faithful. God has given each of us gifts: a smile, a talent, time, a kind heart. We are not to hide them, but to use them to help others.
family.intention: We thank God for the gifts of each person in our family, and we ask the Lord to show us how to use them for our parish and our neighbours. We also remember Saint Maria Goretti, a girl who forgave.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one gift each of us has that we could use this week to help someone?”

illus: An illustration

In a village near Kuravilangad (a story told to illustrate the reading) a retired gulf worker named Joseph returned after thirty years with a modest sum in the bank. His neighbour, Kuriakose, had inherited the same amount and had put it into a steel trunk under his bed ‘for safety’. Joseph rented a small room next to the church and began an evening class without fees for children whose parents worked in the rubber estates; two young teachers joined him, then more. After seven years sixty children came every evening, and several had become nurses and engineers. Kuriakose, in the same years, watched his trunk, and when he opened it the notes were eaten by silverfish. At Joseph's farewell function Kuriakose said quietly, ‘I was so afraid of losing it that I lost it all.’ Joseph answered, ‘I was afraid too, Kuriakose. But I was more afraid of dying without having used it.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you entrusted your gifts to us and will come again. Gather us, and make us faithful servants who trade with what you have given. Amen.
share: Be infants in evil, but in thinking be adults (1 Corinthians 14:20). Where do I need more innocence, and where more wisdom?
God is really among you (1 Corinthians 14:25). What would a stranger see in my parish and in my family?
Do business with these until I come back (Luke 19:13). What has the Lord entrusted to me, and what have I done with it?
I was afraid of you (Luke 19:21). What picture of God makes me hide my gifts?
pm.resp: Lord, make us faithful in a very little.
interc: For all who lead worship and teach the faith, that the word may be understood and touch the heart.
For the gifts of our parish: for its volunteers, choir, catechists and visitors, that they may build up the Church.
For young people, that like Saint Maria Goretti they may choose what is good and pure.
For victims of violence and abuse, that they may find healing, justice and mercy.
For ourselves, that we may not bury our gifts but use them in love.
pm.close: Father, you give every gift and you will return in glory. Make us trustworthy in small things, bold in using your gifts, pure in heart and quick to forgive, so that we may hear your word, “Well done, good and trustworthy servant.” Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: man of God, run from the love of money and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance and gentleness.
Paul: fight the good fight, take hold of eternal life, and keep the commandment until the Lord appears.
John: the sheep hear his voice, are known by him, follow him, and no one can snatch them from his hand.
2027-07-07.action: Begin tomorrow with five minutes of silence and the Gospel of the day, before any screen.
2027-07-07.question: Whose voice do I follow when I am tired, afraid or tempted?

family.explain: Jesus is like a shepherd, and we are his sheep. A good shepherd knows each sheep by name, and the sheep know his voice. When many people are calling, the sheep walk towards the voice they know. Jesus says that nobody can take us out of his hand.
family.intention: We pray for children who feel lost or lonely, and for our priests, who are shepherds in the name of Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How do we learn to know the voice of Jesus in our house?”

illus: An illustration

In a hill village in Idukki (a story told to illustrate the reading) a grandfather was called every evening to bring the cows home from the slope. The children noticed that he never shouted or used a stick. He stood at the edge of the field and gave one low call that nobody else used. The cows, which stood in a crowd of other cattle after the rains, lifted their heads, separated from the herd and walked to him. A grandson asked how they knew. He said, ‘I have fed them from my hand since they were calves. They know whose voice brings food and not trouble.’ That night, when the family knelt for prayer, the boy asked, ‘Is that what the shepherd in the Gospel means?’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, we are your flock. Speak to us now, and let us hear you, and follow where you lead. Amen.
share: Fight the good fight of the faith (1 Timothy 6:12). Where is my struggle today, and with whom am I really fighting?
Pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, gentleness (1 Timothy 6:11). Which of the six is weakest in me?
How long will you keep us in suspense? (John 10:24). Where do I ask God for a sign when he has already spoken?
My sheep hear my voice (John 10:27). When did I last hear it clearly, and what did it ask of me?
pm.resp: Lord, we hear your voice; we follow you.
interc: For the Church, that she may keep the faith of the apostles without spot or blame.
For priests, bishops and catechists, that they may be faithful shepherds who know their sheep.
For all who are tired in the good fight: the sick, the old and those who care for them.
For those who have lost their way, that they may hear the voice of the Shepherd.
For our families, that every home may be a place where his voice is heard.
pm.close: Father, you gave us your Son as our Shepherd and our King. Keep us in his hand and bring us to the eternal life he promised, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: pray and sing with the spirit and with the mind; in the Church, five words that instruct are better than ten thousand in a tongue.
Paul: the Amen of the people must be able to follow the prayer; the gift is for the building up of the Church.
John: Jesus honours the Father, Abraham rejoiced to see his day, and before Abraham was, I am.
2027-07-08.action: At the next Holy Qurbana say every Amen slowly, with understanding, and offer one of them for someone who is ill.
2027-07-08.question: Do I say my Amen as words I mean, or by habit?

family.explain: Paul tells us to pray with our heart and with our mind together. When the priest prays in church, everyone says “Amen”. Amen means: yes, this is true, and I agree! Jesus said a surprising thing about himself: he was there before Abraham was born. Jesus is as old as God, because he is God's Son.
family.intention: We pray for our parish church, for the choir and the altar servers, and for all who help us to pray at the Qurbana.
family.ask: Ask: “What do we mean when we say Amen at the end of our prayer?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish near Kottayam (a story told to illustrate the reading) an old woman who had never gone beyond the fourth standard sat in the second row every day. After the Qurbana a young catechist asked her what she liked best. ‘The Amen,’ she said. ‘All my life I could not read the big books, but I could say Amen, and I always knew what I was agreeing to, because the priest said it in the language of my home.’ The catechist wrote it in his notebook. Years later he told his students, ‘She taught me what Paul means: if the Amen is understood, the person who says it is built up, and the whole parish with her.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the great I AM, and you are here among us. Open our minds and our hearts, and let our Amen be true. Amen.
share: I will pray with the spirit, but I will pray with the mind also (1 Corinthians 14:15). Which do I neglect more, the heart or the mind?
How can anyone say the Amen if they do not know what you are saying? (1 Corinthians 14:16). Do I help others to pray, or leave them outside?
Whoever keeps my word will never see death (John 8:51). Which word of his am I not keeping?
Before Abraham was, I am (John 8:58). What does it mean to me that Jesus is God?
pm.resp: Lord, we believe; you are the I AM.
interc: For our parish and the choirs, readers and servers, that all our prayer may be understood and answered by all.
For people who do not understand the language of the worship around them: migrants, the elderly and the hard of hearing.
For Jewish and Christian neighbours, that hatred may end and respect may grow.
For all who have lost the joy of prayer, that they may find it again.
For ourselves, that we may keep his word and live.
pm.close: Father, your Son is before all ages and is with us still. Make our prayer true and our Amen faithful, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Isaiah: God has chosen Jacob; do not fear, for I am with you and will uphold you with my right hand.
Acts and Paul: the name of Jesus is not a charm; burn the books of magic; our weapons are divine and are for building up.
Luke: do not fear those who kill the body; not one sparrow is forgotten; acknowledge Christ, and the Spirit will teach you what to say.
2027-07-09.action: Set aside one fear this week and say to the Lord, ‘You are with me,’ each time it returns.
2027-07-09.question: In whom do I really trust when I am afraid?

family.explain: Jesus tells us that God does not forget even one little sparrow, and that he has counted every hair on our head. So we do not need to be afraid. Today we remember a bishop named Mar Yakob, who lived a very long time ago in a city called Nisibis. He prayed and taught the children, and one of his students, Ephrem, became a great singer of God's praise.
family.intention: We pray for Christians in countries where it is dangerous to say that they love Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What are we afraid of, and how can we give it to Jesus in our prayer?”

illus: An illustration

A young nurse in a mission hospital in Wayanad (a story told to illustrate the reading) was afraid of the monsoon night duty: the river rose, the lights went, and a woman in labour was brought in on a jeep. Her old matron, a Sister of seventy, said only, ‘Do you know how many sparrows are sold for two pennies?’ and went on counting the contractions with her hand on the patient's wrist. By morning the child was born and the road had been cleared. ‘I was not afraid when she said that,’ the nurse said later. ‘Not that the danger was small, but that I was counted.’ She still keeps a small card with the sparrow verse in her uniform pocket.

pm.open: God of Jacob and of Mar Yakob, you tell us not to fear, for you are with us. Strengthen us with your right hand, and teach us what to say. Amen.
share: Do not fear, for I am with you (Isaiah 41:10). What fear do I bring to him today?
Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are you? (Acts 19:15). Do I use the name of Jesus, or do I belong to him?
The weapons of our warfare are not merely human (2 Corinthians 10:4). What are my weapons when I am hurt or angry?
Everyone who acknowledges me before others (Luke 12:8). Where do I stay silent about my faith?
pm.resp: Lord, we do not fear; you are with us.
interc: For the Church of the East and for all Christians in the lands where Mar Yakob lived, that they may live in peace.
For Christians who suffer persecution, that they may bear witness without fear.
For all who are afraid tonight: the sick, the lonely and those who face the storm and flood.
For catechists and teachers, that they may build up and not tear down.
For ourselves, that we may trust Christ alone.
pm.close: Father, you do not forget one sparrow. Keep us in your love and give us the courage of your martyrs and saints, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: refuse partnership with idols and sin; we are the temple of the living God, and God will be our Father.
Mark: four friends carry a paralysed man, dig through the roof, and Jesus sees their faith.
Mark: Jesus forgives the man's sins first, then heals him, to show that the Son of Man has authority to forgive.
2027-07-10.action: Carry one person to Jesus this week by name: pray, visit, and offer your Holy Qurbana for them.
2027-07-10.question: Who is on a mat in my life, and am I one of the four who carry?

family.explain: Some friends wanted to bring their sick friend to Jesus, but the house was full. So they climbed up, made a hole in the roof, and let him down to Jesus! Jesus saw how much they believed. He forgave the man's sins and made him walk. Good friends carry each other to Jesus. And Jesus lives in us, as in a temple.
family.intention: We pray for friends who are sick, and for those who help them.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is a friend that we can carry to Jesus by our prayer this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a village in Pathanamthitta (a story told to illustrate the reading) four young men from the parish youth group used to carry old Kunjamma, who had lost the use of her legs, to church in a plastic chair every Sunday. The road was muddy in the rains, and twice they slipped. One day a visitor asked why they did it, since she could pray at home. ‘She cannot walk,’ said one, ‘but she has prayed for each of us since we were babies. We are only returning the favour.’ The old woman, when asked, said, ‘They carry my chair; I carry their names to the altar.’ On the feast day the parish priest wrote on the notice board: ‘Four men and a chair: a parish.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, we bring to you those we love who are weak and burdened. See our faith, and say to them and to us: your sins are forgiven. Amen.
share: We are the temple of the living God (2 Corinthians 6:16). How do I treat my body and my home as his dwelling place?
Come out from them, and be separate (2 Corinthians 6:17). What partnership in sin must I leave?
When Jesus saw their faith (Mark 2:5). Whom do I carry to Jesus, and who carries me?
Who can forgive sins but God alone? (Mark 2:7). When did I last receive his forgiveness in the sacrament?
pm.resp: Lord, forgive us and heal us.
interc: For the sick and paralysed, in body or in spirit, that they may be carried to Christ.
For the families and friends who carry them, that they may not tire.
For priests who forgive in the name of Christ, that they may be faithful ministers of mercy.
For those who feel unforgivable, that they may hear: Son, daughter, your sins are forgiven.
For Mary's children everywhere, that on this Saturday they may learn from her to carry others to Jesus.
pm.close: Father, your Son forgives sins and heals the whole person. Make us his dwelling place and servants of his mercy, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: James: blessed is the one who endures; God tempts no one; desire gives birth to sin and sin to death.
James: every good gift comes from the Father of lights, who does not change; he has given us birth by the word of truth, as first fruits.
Matthew: not those who say Lord, Lord but those who do the Father's will; the wise man builds his house on rock, and acts on the words.
2027-07-12.action: Choose one word of Jesus and put it into practice at home today, in a visible, small deed.
2027-07-12.question: What is the foundation of my house, and what happens to it in a storm?

family.explain: Jesus told us about two builders. One built his house on rock, and the other built his on sand. When the rain and the floods and the wind came, the house on the rock stood, but the house on the sand fell down. The rock means listening to Jesus and doing what he says. Every time we obey Jesus, our family house becomes stronger.
family.intention: We pray for families who lost their houses in floods and landslides, and for those who build and repair houses.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing Jesus asked us to do that our family can do this week?”

illus: An illustration

A mason in Kuttanad (a story told to illustrate the reading), who rebuilt houses after the 2018 floods, always insisted on digging down to the hard soil before laying a single stone, even when the owner was in a hurry and wanted to see walls. ‘The wall that people see is a month's work,’ he would say, ‘the part they do not see is where the house is saved or lost.’ A young helper once asked why he took so long over the foundation. The mason pointed to a house nearby that had shifted after one heavy rain. ‘That one hurried,’ he said. When the next flood came, his houses stood with water around them. The helper, who had joined the church choir that year, said afterwards, ‘Now I understand the Gospel about the rock; I only had not seen it with my own hands.’

pm.open: Father of lights, giver of every good gift, you do not change. Teach us to hear your word and do it, and let our house stand on the rock. Amen.
share: Blessed is anyone who endures temptation (James 1:12). What trial am I enduring now, and how can I stay faithful in it?
Desire gives birth to sin (James 1:15). Which desire is growing in me, and what is the first step I can take against it?
Every perfect gift is from above (James 1:17). Which gifts have I forgotten to thank him for?
Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord’ (Matthew 7:21). What do I say to the Lord, and what do I actually do?
pm.resp: Lord, give us the grace to hear and to do.
interc: For those in trial and temptation, that they may endure and receive the crown of life.
For young people, that they may be saved from the first bait of sin.
For families rebuilding after floods and storms, that they may be supported.
For preachers and teachers, that their lives may match their words.
For ourselves, that we may build our houses on the rock of his word.
pm.close: Father, you have given us birth by the word of truth. Make us hear it and do it, until we stand with you for ever, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: James: our fights come from cravings within; friendship with the world is enmity with God; God gives grace to the humble.
Luke: blessed are the poor, the hungry, the weeping and the hated for the Son of Man; woe to the rich, the full, the laughing and the praised.
Together: the one who owns the kingdom does not need to quarrel for scraps.
2027-07-13.action: Make the first move toward peace with one person with whom you have quarrelled, and pray for them by name.
2027-07-13.question: What am I fighting for, and have I asked God for it?

family.explain: Jesus looked at his friends and said: blessed are you who are poor, you who are hungry, you who cry. Why blessed? Because God is close to them and the kingdom of God is theirs. Jesus does not mean that being hungry is good. He means that God never forgets the one who has nothing, and that those who trust him will be filled. And he asks us to be like him and to share what we have, so that nobody in our village goes to bed hungry.
family.intention: We pray for families who are poor, for those who are quarrelling, and for the people who share their food with others.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there somebody in our street or parish whom we can help this week with food, a visit or a kind word?”

illus: An illustration

In a village near Changanassery (a story told to illustrate the reading) two brothers had not spoken for eleven years because of a boundary stone between their rubber plots. The case dragged through the court, and each brother told his sons never to give way. One July night the river rose, and both families had to climb to the parish hall. The brothers found themselves on the same mat, wet and ashamed, with their old mother between them. In the morning the water had gone down, and the boundary stone was gone with it. The elder brother looked at the field and said quietly, ‘The water has done in one night what the court could not do in eleven years.’ The younger poured him a cup of tea. Nobody mentioned the stone again.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you called the poor blessed and gave your Church the kingdom as an inheritance. Gather us now; heal what is at war in us and among us, and make us humble enough to receive your grace. Amen.
share: Those conflicts and disputes among you, where do they come from? (James 4:1). What is the real source of the quarrel I carry?
God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble (James 4:6). Where do I need to bend my pride this week?
Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God (Luke 6:20). What do I cling to that I should hold more lightly?
Woe to you when all speak well of you (Luke 6:26). Do I fear the opinion of people more than the judgment of God?
pm.resp: Lord, give us your grace and make us humble.
interc: For the families in our parish who are divided by quarrels over property or old wounds, that the Lord may bring them to peace.
For the poor, the hungry and those who weep, that they may be filled and comforted, and that we may not forget them.
For those who preach and lead, that they may not seek the praise of people more than the truth.
For Christians who are hated and reviled for the name of Jesus, that they may rejoice and stand firm.
For ourselves, that we may ask rightly, share gladly and submit to God.
pm.close: Father, you give grace to the humble and the kingdom to the poor. Keep us from the cravings that divide us, and lead us to the joy of your kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Paul: the One who raised Jesus will raise us; our outer nature wastes away, our inner nature is renewed day by day; the earthly tent will give way to a house from God.
John: the hour has come; the grain of wheat must die to bear fruit; whoever serves Jesus must follow him.
Together: what looks like loss in the soil of faith becomes a harvest.
2027-07-14.action: Offer one small dying to self today, and visit or call someone who is old or sick.
2027-07-14.question: Am I keeping my life in a tin, or am I letting it fall into the earth for others?

family.explain: Jesus said: a grain of wheat must fall into the ground and die, and then it grows into many grains. When the farmer plants a seed in the wet earth, it looks as if the seed is lost. But after some days a green shoot comes up, and later there is a whole field. Jesus told us this about himself: he died on the Cross, and then he rose, and now so many people believe in him all over the world. And he asks us to be like seeds that give themselves for others.
family.intention: We pray for our grandparents and for all who are old or sick, and for our dear ones who have died.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one small thing we can give up this week so that someone else can be happy?”

illus: An illustration

An old farmer in Kuttanad (a story told to illustrate the reading) used to keep the best of his seed paddy in a tin on the shelf above the bed. His grandson, who was about eight, once asked why the old man took the finest grains out in the rains and pushed them into the black mud. ‘If I keep them in the tin, they stay safe, and they stay one grain,’ said the old man. ‘If I put them in the mud, I lose them for a while, and then I get a field.’ Years later, when the old man died in the month of Karkidakam, the family found the empty tin on the shelf with a slip of paper inside, in his shaky hand: ‘Do not keep it. Sow it.’ The grandson, who had become a teacher, copied the words and pinned them above the door of his classroom.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you went to your hour and gave yourself like a grain of wheat. Gather us now, and let our weakness and our hope be offered with you to the Father. Amen.
share: We do not lose heart (2 Corinthians 4:16). What discourages me most, and can I place it in the hands of the One who raised Jesus?
Our inner nature is being renewed day by day (2 Corinthians 4:16). What helps my inner life grow: prayer, the Qurbana, silence, service?
We look not at what can be seen but at what cannot be seen (2 Corinthians 4:18). What do I give too much weight to that will not last?
Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies (John 12:24). Where is God asking me to let go so that something can grow?
pm.resp: Lord, make us a grain that bears fruit.
interc: For the sick, the elderly and all whose bodies are wasting away, that their inner strength may be renewed day by day.
For the dead of our families and parish, that God may give them the house not made with hands.
For martyrs and for Christians who suffer for the faith, that their blood may be a seed of life.
For farmers, who sow and wait through the rains, that the harvest may be sufficient for all.
For ourselves, that we may have the courage to die to ourselves and to bear fruit.
pm.close: Father, you glorified your name in the death and resurrection of your Son. Make our lives fruitful for the good of others and bring us at last to the house not made with hands. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Carmel: Elijah prays seven times, and a little cloud brings the rain; Isaiah sings of Carmel's splendour; Paul speaks of the God of all consolation.
Luke: a woman blesses the womb that bore Jesus, and Jesus says, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it!” Mary is first among them.
Mar Mari: disciple of Mar Addai, missionary of the East; the readings speak of the word that does not return empty, and of the Risen Lord who sends his apostles.
2027-07-16.action: Bring one unanswered prayer to God again each day this week, and keep one line of the coming Sunday's Gospel.
2027-07-16.question: Is the house of my heart swept and put in order, and is it filled with the word of God?

family.explain: Elijah the prophet went up a mountain called Carmel to pray for rain, because the fields were dry. He asked his friend to look at the sea. The friend looked once: nothing. He looked again, and again: nothing. At the seventh time he said, “I see a little cloud, as small as a hand.” And soon the whole sky was dark, and the rain came down! Our Lady of Mount Carmel loves us, and she teaches us to keep praying and to listen to Jesus. And long ago Mar Mari and Mar Addai went to far countries to tell people about Jesus, so that the Gospel could reach even us.
family.intention: We pray to Our Lady of Mount Carmel for our family, for those who pray and wait, and for missionaries who tell people about Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there a prayer we have almost stopped praying? Shall we pray it again tonight, together?”

illus: An illustration

In a village near Pala (a story told to illustrate the reading) a mother prayed every evening for her son, who had gone abroad, stopped coming to church and stopped answering her calls. She wore the brown scapular, and every Friday she said the rosary before the picture of Our Lady of Mount Carmel and then stood at the gate and looked down the road. Month after month there was nothing. Like Elijah's servant she looked again, and again, and sometimes she was ashamed that she was still looking. On the eve of the feast, in the fifth year, a message came on her old phone: ‘Amma, I am coming home for the feast. Will there be fish curry?’ It was only a few words, ‘a little cloud no bigger than a hand’. She showed it to the whole parish, and on the feast day, after the Holy Qurbana, the whole village saw that the rain had come.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Son of Mary, you called blessed those who hear the word of God and keep it. Gather us now at the foot of Carmel; teach us to wait, to listen, and to console. Through the prayer of your Mother, hear us. Amen.
share: Elijah went up to the top of Carmel and bowed himself down upon the earth (1 Kings 18:42). What prayer do I need to bring to God again, on my knees?
Look, a little cloud no bigger than a person's hand (1 Kings 18:44). Where in my life do I see a sign, small as it is, that God has heard?
Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it (Luke 11:28). Which word of God have I heard this week and not yet done?
The Father of mercies and the God of all consolation (2 Corinthians 1:3). Whom can I console with the comfort I have received?
pm.resp: Holy Mary of Carmel, pray for us.
interc: For the Carmelite fathers, brothers and sisters of our Church, especially the CMI and CMC families, that they may be faithful to the prayer and mission of Carmel.
For all who wear the scapular and all who honour Mary, that they may hear the word of God and obey it.
For those who wait for an answer to a long prayer, that they may see the little cloud and not lose heart.
For the Church of the East and all who pray the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, that the apostolic faith may be kept and handed on.
For those who grieve and are afflicted, that the God of all consolation may comfort them through us.
pm.close: Father, you gave us Mary as a mother and Elijah as a teacher of prayer. Hear us as you heard them, and let your word dwell in us until the whole earth is green. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: James: favouritism toward the rich in the assembly breaks the royal law of love; God has chosen the poor to be rich in faith and heirs of the kingdom.
Luke: the great dinner; the invited make excuses; the poor, the crippled, the blind and the lame are brought in; “there is still room”.
Together: God's table is open to all, and his invitation cannot wait on our business.
2027-07-17.action: Greet and sit beside a person at the next parish gathering whom others overlook.
2027-07-17.question: What excuse do I give when God says, “Come; everything is ready now”?

family.explain: Once a man made a big dinner and invited many friends. But when he said, “Come, everything is ready,” they all made excuses: one had to see his new field, one had to try his new oxen, one had just been married. The man was sad, and he said to his servant, “Go to the streets and invite the poor and the lame and the blind!” And the servant said, “There is still room.” That is how God is: he asks everybody to his house, and he loves those whom nobody invites. We can do the same: we can invite the child who sits alone, the old neighbour, the family that has little.
family.intention: We pray for the poor, the lonely and the stranger, and for the house of God to be full.
family.ask: Ask: “Whom shall we invite to our table this week, someone who cannot invite us back?”

illus: An illustration

At a parish feast near Kanjirappally (a story told to illustrate the reading) the council had put up two long tables in the hall for the feast-day lunch, with a smaller table for the guests of honour. At the gate stood an old man in a torn shirt, a scrap collector named Velu, who had come to ask for some water. A young trustee saw him and looked at the hall. ‘There is no room,’ he started to say, and then he stopped, because the vicar had been preaching that morning on the great dinner. He picked up his plate from the guests' table, went to the gate and said, ‘Velu chettan, there is still room. Please sit here.’ The old man shook his head, laughing; but when he was seated, an elderly widow passed him the rice without a word, and the lady next to her filled his glass. The vicar later told the story at the next Sunday Qurbana, and wrote on the notice-board in his own hand: ‘There is still room.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you invite everyone to the supper of your kingdom. Gather us in the same assembly, rich and poor together, and open our hearts to hear your call without delay. Amen.
share: Do you with your acts of favoritism really believe in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ? (James 2:1). Whom do I treat better, and whom do I overlook?
Has not God chosen the poor in the world to be rich in faith? (James 2:5). What have the poor taught me about faith?
They all alike began to make excuses (Luke 14:18). Which good thing have I put before God's call?
There is still room (Luke 14:22). Whom can I bring to the Lord's table?
pm.resp: Lord, make room in our hearts for all.
interc: For the poor, the lonely and the strangers in our parishes, that they may be welcomed first at the table of the Church.
For priests and parish councils, that they may keep the doors of the Church open to all without favouritism.
For those who put work, wealth or family before God's call, that they may answer his invitation.
For those who have never heard the Gospel and for all who are still outside the house, that the Lord may fill it.
For ourselves, that we may love our neighbour as ourselves.
pm.close: Father, you prepare a table for all peoples and you ask us to make room. Make us welcoming in your house and ready to answer your call. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: James: Abraham's faith was brought to completion by his obedience; Rahab's welcome of the messengers shows faith at work; faith without works is dead.
Matthew: Jesus sends prophets and wise men and scribes, warns of the cost of refusing them, and laments over Jerusalem like a hen who would gather her chicks.
Together: a living faith is a faith that obeys and welcomes, and the Lord is always the one who gathers.
2027-07-19.action: Do one act of faith this week that costs you something: a visit, a gift, a pardon.
2027-07-19.question: What fruit does my faith bear, and where have I been unwilling to be gathered?

family.explain: Rahab opened her door to two strangers and helped them, and God remembered her kindness. James tells us that believing in God and doing good go together, like a body and its breath. Jesus said he wanted to gather the people of Jerusalem like a mother hen gathers her chicks under her wings. Think of the chicks hurrying under the hen when a kite flies over: that is how safe we are with Jesus.
family.intention: We thank God for the people who sheltered us when we were small, and we pray for the lonely and for strangers who need a door opened.
family.ask: Ask: “Whose door can our family open this week, and how?”

illus: An illustration

In a village near Kottayam (a story told to illustrate the reading) an old woman was known for saying her rosary on the front verandah every evening. One monsoon night the river rose and the poor house across the lane filled with water. She put down her beads, took a lantern, and went out into the rain with her grandsons; they carried the neighbours' mats and pots to her own verandah, and the family slept in her kitchen for a week. When the parish priest thanked her, she smiled and said, ‘The rosary brought me as far as the door. Then the door had to open.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you would gather us as a hen gathers her chicks. We come under your wings. Open our eyes to see what our faith asks of us today. Amen.
share: Abraham's faith was brought to completion by his works (James 2:22). Where is my faith still only in words?
Rahab welcomed the messengers (James 2:25). Whom could I welcome who is a stranger to me?
How often have I desired to gather your children (Matthew 23:37). When have I felt the Lord gathering me and I was unwilling?
You will not see me again until you say, Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord (Matthew 23:39). How do I welcome the Lord when he comes in the poor and the stranger?
pm.resp: Lord, gather us under your wings.
interc: For the Church, that her faith may be seen in works of mercy.
For the Jewish people, our elder brothers and sisters in faith, that God who called them will keep faith with them, and for peace between all peoples.
For those who have no home or shelter in this monsoon season.
For those whose faith has grown cold, that they may feel the Lord gathering them.
For ourselves, that our faith may bear fruit in good works.
pm.close: Father, you gather your children in Christ and ask for the obedience of faith. Make us alive in faith and generous in works, until we are gathered at last into your house. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: James: wisdom is shown by a good life; earthly wisdom brings envy and disorder; wisdom from above is pure, peaceable and merciful; a harvest of righteousness is sown in peace.
Luke: at Nazareth Jesus reads Isaiah and is rejected as Joseph's son; he recalls Elijah and the widow of Zarephath, Elisha and Naaman, and the crowd drives him out.
Together: envy and familiarity close our eyes to God's work; peace opens them.
2027-07-20.action: Congratulate someone this week whose success you secretly envy, and mean it.
2027-07-20.question: Where do envy or familiarity keep me from seeing what God is doing?

family.explain: Jesus came to his own town, Nazareth. The people there thought: we know him, he is only Joseph's son! They would not believe in him. Saint James tells us what God's wisdom looks like: it is gentle and peaceful and full of kindness. When someone else gets a prize or a gift and we feel a little sad, that is called envy. God's wisdom helps us to be happy for them instead.
family.intention: We thank God for the good things that others receive, and we pray for peace in our homes, our school and our village.
family.ask: Ask: “Who can we congratulate this week, and how?”

illus: An illustration

In a village near Changanassery (a story told to illustrate the reading) a young man became a doctor in the city and came home to start a small clinic. The old people of the village still remembered him as the boy who climbed their mango trees, and for months they walked three miles to another town to see a stranger. His old catechism teacher said to him gently one evening, ‘We find it hard to see a doctor in the child we scolded.’ The young man smiled and began to visit each house with a flask of hot tea for the elders. Slowly the clinic filled, and the teacher said at the Sunday service, ‘We were slow to see what God had given us in our own village.’

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were not accepted in your own town, yet you came to all. Give us the wisdom from above, and open our eyes to see you in those we know best. Amen.
share: Who is wise and understanding among you? Show it by your good life (James 3:13). What would others see in my works today?
Where there is envy and selfish ambition there is disorder (James 3:16). Where do I feel envy, and what does it do to my relationships?
The wisdom from above is pure, peaceable, gentle (James 3:17). Which of these marks do I most need to ask for?
Is not this Joseph's son? (Luke 4:22). Whom do I take for granted, so that I do not see what God gives through them?
pm.resp: Lord, give us the wisdom from above.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a community of peace, without envy or ambition.
For parish councils, committees and families, that disputes may be settled in gentleness.
For prophets and teachers who are not welcomed in their own places.
