Christ wants to live in your heart, not to visit it. A tree planted by a stream does not fear the heat, because its roots are deep. A house with a deep foundation stands in the flood. So the love of Christ is the ground where our life stands.

Paul speaks of the breadth, length, height and depth of Christ's love. Saint Augustine said that this is the Cross, which stretches its arms to the whole world. On this Friday we remember that nothing can be too wide, too long, too high or too deep for the love of Christ: not our worst sin, not our deepest sorrow.

In the Gospel Jesus heals a blind man in two steps. The first time the man sees people like trees walking, and Jesus does not scold him. He touches his eyes again, and the man sees everything clearly (Mark 8:25). The Lord is patient with our dim sight.
This week let us kneel for our family each evening, bring someone to Jesus by prayer, and ask him to touch our eyes again where we see only a little. Amen.
kids: Children, a man could not see. His friends brought him to Jesus. Jesus touched his eyes, and the man saw people like trees walking! So Jesus touched him again, and then he could see everything. Jesus is never in a hurry with us. Let us bring our friends to Jesus by our prayers, and ask him to help us see how much he loves us!

homily: Dear friends, you have seen the mist on the hills in the morning. It is thick, and then it is gone. Saint James says that our life is like that: “You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes” (James 4:14).

So he gives us a lesson: when we plan, we should say, “If the Lord wishes, we will live and do this or that” (James 4:15). We may plan, but we are not the lords of tomorrow. And he adds a sentence for each of us: “Anyone, then, who knows the right thing to do and fails to do it, commits sin” (James 4:17). What good do you know and keep putting off?

In the Gospel John tells Jesus: “We tried to stop him, because he does not follow with us.” Jesus replies: “Do not stop him; for whoever is not against you is for you” (Luke 9:49–50). God is glad when anyone does good in his name. Let us not be jealous of other people's good works.

Then Jesus sets his face toward Jerusalem. A village refuses him, and James and John want fire from heaven. Jesus rebukes them, and they go on to another village (Luke 9:55–56). The Lord is gentle; he does not take revenge, because he is going to the Cross for us.
This week let us offer our plans to God, do one good thing that we have put off, and say a thank-you for someone's good work. Amen.
kids: Children, have you seen mist on the hills? In the morning it is thick and white, and then the sun comes and it is gone! Our life is like that, so we must always do good today and say, “If God wishes.” And if you see someone who is not your friend doing good, do not stop them: clap for them! Jesus says: whoever is not against us is for us.

homily: Dear friends, yesterday we honoured grandparents and the elderly. Today the Church remembers the most famous grandparents in the world: Saint Joachim and Saint Anne, the parents of the Virgin Mary and the grandparents of Jesus. The Bible does not give their names. They come from an early Christian tradition. But the Church has loved them for centuries.

The first reading gives us the song of Hannah, a woman who could not have a child and who prayed with all her heart. When God gave her a son she sang: “He raises up the poor from the dust; he lifts the needy from the ash heap” (1 Samuel 2:8). Mary would sing a song just like this in the Magnificat. According to the old tradition, Joachim and Anne also prayed for a child for a long time. God heard them.

The letter to the Hebrews tells us of Abraham and Sarah, who were too old to have children, and yet God made them parents of a great people because they trusted his promise (Hebrews 11:11–12). Faith means trusting the one who keeps promises, even when our own strength is gone.

The Gospel is a list of names: “An account of the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah” (Matthew 1:1). It tells us that Jesus was born into a human family, with ancestors and grandparents. In our families, too, faith comes down through the generations: the grandmother who lights the lamp, the grandfather who takes us to church, the parents who teach us to pray. We are links in that chain.

The weekday readings add a warning. Saint James tells the rich: “Your riches have rotted” (James 5:2). And Jesus says what is impossible for us is possible for God (Luke 18:27). Let us not trust money. Let us thank God for our grandparents, pray for them, and hand on the faith to our children. Saints Joachim and Anne, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, do you know who Mary's mummy and daddy were? Their names were Joachim and Anne, and they were Jesus' grandparents! They loved God and prayed a lot. Today, hug your grandparents, or if they are in heaven, say a little prayer: ‘Thank you, God, for my grandparents.’

homily: Dear friends, in Kerala we know what it is to wait for rain. The farmer repairs his bund, keeps the seed ready, and looks at the sky. He cannot make the rain come. Saint James uses this picture today: “Be patient, therefore, beloved, until the coming of the Lord. The farmer waits for the precious crop from the earth, being patient with it until it receives the early and the late rains” (James 5:7).

Patience is not laziness. It is strength of heart: “Strengthen your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is near” (James 5:8). James gives three practical rules for the waiting time. Do not grumble against one another. Learn endurance from the prophets and from Job, who said, “the Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord” (Job 1:21). And keep your word: let your ‘Yes’ be yes and your ‘No’ be no (James 5:12).

In the Gospel Jesus speaks about his coming in glory. The sun darkens and the stars fall, which is the language of the Bible for the end of one age and the beginning of another. But in the middle of it all there is one sure thing: “Then they will see ‘the Son of Man coming in clouds’ with great power and glory” (Mark 13:26). And he will gather his chosen ones from the ends of the earth, even from the smallest village on the farthest hill.

Jesus gives us a lesson from the fig tree: when the branch becomes tender and puts out leaves, you know that summer is near (Mark 13:28). The signs are small: a leaf, a kind word, a prayer in a hard time. We do not know the day or the hour; the Father alone knows. So Jesus says: “keep alert” (Mark 13:33).

And then the promise: “Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away” (Mark 13:31). The monsoon passes, the years pass, we pass; his word remains. So let us wait like the farmer: busy, trusting, without grumbling, saying every day: Come, Lord Jesus. Amen.
kids: Children, when a farmer plants seeds, he must wait for the rain. He cannot make it come, but he does not stop working. Jesus wants us to wait for him in the same way: be patient, be kind, do not grumble, and keep your promises. Jesus will come again, and his words will never pass away. Say with me: Come, Lord Jesus!

homily: Dear friends, today is the feast of a daughter of our own land, Saint Alphonsa. Anna was born in 1910 at Kudamaloor, near Kottayam. Her mother died when she was a baby, and she grew up with her mother's sister. She loved prayer. She longed to belong to Jesus. In 1927 she entered the convent of the Clarist sisters at Bharananganam, where she took the name Alphonsa. She was often ill, and she died on 28 July 1946, when she was only thirty-five. In 2008 Pope Benedict XVI declared her a saint, the first woman of Indian origin to be so honoured.

What made her a saint? The Gospel today gives the answer. Some Greeks come to Philip and say, “Sir, we wish to see Jesus.” And Jesus says: “unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit” (John 12:24). A grain that stays in the bag is safe, but it gives no harvest. A grain that falls into the earth seems to disappear, but it gives life to many.

Alphonsa was such a grain. She lived in a small convent, she was often sick, she did simple tasks. Nobody in the world noticed her. But she gave everything, her pain and her prayer, to Jesus. Today thousands come to pray at her tomb, and millions know her name. Saint Paul says the same: “I have been crucified with Christ; and it is no longer I who live, but it is Christ who lives in me” (Galatians 2:19–20).

Let us not misunderstand. Suffering is not good in itself; we should treat the sick and remove pain as far as we can. But when suffering comes, and it comes to every home, we can join it to the cross of Jesus. Saint Paul says: “in my flesh I am completing what is lacking in Christ’s afflictions for the sake of his body, that is, the church” (Colossians 1:24). Our pain, offered in love, is never wasted.

We are in the season of Kaitha, the season of harvest. Jesus looks at the crowds and says: “The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few” (Matthew 9:37). Saint Alphonsa was one of the laborers, though she worked from a sickbed. Today let us pray for more laborers, let us visit someone who is sick or alone, and let us offer one small pain for someone we love. Saint Alphonsa, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, today is the feast of Saint Alphonsa. She was a little girl from Kerala who lost her mother as a baby, and she loved Jesus very much. When she was sick or when something hurt, she did not complain, and she gave it to Jesus. Jesus said that a seed must fall into the earth to grow into a plant. Alphonsa was like a seed, and she gave a lot of love to the world. When something is hard for you, say: ‘Jesus, I give this to you.’

homily: Dear friends, today the Church remembers Saint Martha, the friend of Jesus. We know her from three scenes. In Luke she is the busy woman who welcomes Jesus into her home and cooks for him. In John she is the sister who runs to meet Jesus when her brother has died. At the supper in Bethany, “Martha served.” The Gospel of John says: “Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus” (John 11:5).

The Gospel today is one of the most beautiful of all. Lazarus has been four days in the tomb. Martha hears that Jesus is coming and goes out to meet him. Her words are full of grief and trust: “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died. But even now I know that God will give you whatever you ask of him” (John 11:21–22). And Jesus answers: “I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live, and everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?” (John 11:25–26).

This is the heart of our faith. Resurrection is not only an idea for the last day. It is a person: Jesus himself. And Martha answers, in the next verse: “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, the one coming into the world” (John 11:27). She says it in the middle of her tears. When we stand at a grave, in our own grief, the same question is put to us: Do you believe this?

Saint John writes in the second reading: “Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God… God is love” (1 John 4:7–8). Martha's service was an answer to love. Our hospitality in Kerala, the cup of tea, the meal for the guest, is a way of loving God, if we do it with a heart that is also sitting at the Lord's feet. The Lord does not scold Martha for serving; he asks her not to be “worried and distracted by many things” (Luke 10:41).

The weekday readings say: “Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you” (James 4:8). And Jesus says: “I came to bring fire to the earth” (Luke 12:49), the fire of love. Let us pray today: Lord, light that fire in our homes. Let us serve like Martha and listen like Mary, and answer when he asks: Do you believe this? Saint Martha, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, Martha was a friend of Jesus who lived in Bethany. She cooked and served for him with love. When her brother Lazarus died, she ran to Jesus and said, ‘I believe that you are the Son of God!’ And Jesus brought Lazarus back to life. At home, you can be like Martha: help set the table, welcome guests with a smile. And you can be like Mary too: sit still and say a prayer to Jesus. Say with me: Jesus, I believe!

homily: Dear friends, the Gospel today has a simple question and a simple answer. A lawyer asks Jesus, “Teacher, which commandment in the law is the greatest?” (Matthew 22:36). Jesus answers with two sentences from the Bible that every Jewish child knew: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind. This is the greatest and first commandment. And a second is like it: ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself’” (Matthew 22:37–39).

“On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets” (Matthew 22:40). Think of a door: it hangs on its hinge. Think of a garment: it hangs on a peg. The whole Bible hangs on love. If we have love, we have the whole of what God asks. If we have no love, all the rest is empty. And these two commandments cannot be separated. Saint John says: “Those who say, ‘I love God,’ and hate their brothers or sisters, are liars” (1 John 4:20).

The reading from the letter of James is only three verses. Saint James says: “Let the believer who is lowly boast in being raised up, and the rich in being brought low, because the rich will disappear like a flower in the field” (James 1:9–10). The poor person, whom the world forgets, has the dignity of a child of God. The rich person must remember that money is like grass: green for a season, and then dried by the sun.

We see this in July. After the heavy rain the grass is green and thick, and then the sun comes out in a break of the monsoon, and it begins to dry. Our strength, our money, our position are like that. They are gifts, but they do not last. What lasts is love. And love is not only a feeling; it is a decision to give: time to an old person, food to a hungry neighbour, patience to someone difficult.

In these days we have remembered Saint Alphonsa, Saint Martha, and the grandparents of Jesus. Each of them lived this one commandment in their own way. This week, let us build on the one foundation that does not wash away: love of God and love of neighbour. Amen.
kids: Children, someone asked Jesus: what is the most important thing God wants? And Jesus said: love God with all your heart, and love other people like yourself. If you remember only this, you remember everything! This week, say to God every morning: ‘I love you.’ And share something with a friend or your brother or sister. That is how we keep God's greatest commandment!

homily: Dear friends, today the Church remembers Saint Ignatius of Loyola. He was a soldier in Spain, about five hundred years ago, who loved to dream about glory. At the siege of Pamplona a cannonball broke his leg, and he lay in bed for months. He wanted to read stories of knights, but the house had only a book on the life of Christ and a book on the lives of the saints. He read them, and slowly his heart changed. He left his sword at the altar of Our Lady, and he began a new life. He founded the Society of Jesus, and one of his first friends, Francis Xavier, came to India.

His motto comes from the second reading: “So, whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do everything for the glory of God” (1 Corinthians 10:31). Do everything: eating, working, studying, resting, praying. Ignatius taught us to find God in all things and to offer the whole day to him. Every morning we can say: Lord, today everything for your glory.

The Gospel is demanding. Jesus says that to follow him we must put him first, even before our family, and give up everything that stands in his way (Luke 14:26, 33). He gives two small parables: a man building a tower first counts the cost, and a king going to war first counts his soldiers (Luke 14:28–32). Ignatius counted the cost. He left the court and the comfort and chose Jesus. His prayer says: “Take, Lord, and receive all my liberty, my memory, my understanding and my entire will.”

The weekday readings give two more lessons. In the Gospel, Jesus says: “Have faith in God” (Mark 11:22). Faith and prayer can move mountains. A lame soldier with a few friends started a movement that now serves in nearly every country. And Saint Paul warns the Thessalonians that deception is real, and that the defence against it is the love of the truth (2 Thessalonians 2:10). We need this love in a world of rumours and false messages. Test everything, and hold fast to what is good.
Tomorrow August begins. Let us offer the month to God, saying with Saint Ignatius: for the greater glory of God. Saint Ignatius, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, Saint Ignatius was a soldier whose leg was hurt. In bed he read about Jesus and the saints, and he said, ‘I want to be a soldier for Jesus!’ He started the Jesuits, and his friend Francis Xavier came to India. Ignatius's motto was: for the greater glory of God. Every morning you can say: ‘Jesus, today everything I do is for you.’ Then even brushing your teeth and doing your homework is a prayer!

intro: Theme: “My Lord and my God!”

On the Dukhrana of Saint Thomas the Apostle: the apostle who said “Let us also go”, the Lord who comes again for the one who is missing, the foundation of the apostles, the garden in the east and the path like the light of dawn.

sub: Thomas asks for what the others had received.
Jesus comes again, for one disciple.
The highest confession of the Gospel.
q: Wake up! Bestir yourself for my defense, for my cause, my God and my Lord!
Thomas answered him, “My Lord and my God!”
points.apply: Say “My Lord and my God” in your heart at the elevation in the Qurbana this Sunday.

points.h: Blessed are those who have not seen
sub: We have not seen, yet we believe.
The faith handed on by parents and grandparents.
The Lord comes through closed doors.
q: And he believed the Lord ; and the Lord reckoned it to him as righteousness.
Jesus said to him, “Have you believed because you have seen me? Blessed are those who have not seen and yet have come to believe.”
points.apply: Thank one person, living or dead, who handed the faith on to you.

sub: The Church is built on the apostles.
Thomas, our father in faith, according to tradition.
One heritage, honoured by many Churches.
q: therefore thus says the Lord God , See, I am laying in Zion a foundation stone, a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation
built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Christ Jesus himself as the cornerstone.
points.apply: Learn one fact about the history of your parish and tell it to a child.

sub: God plants a garden and puts the man there to till and keep it.
The river and the tree of life.
The Church, God's garden.
q: The Lord God took the man and put him in the garden of Eden to till it and keep it.

through the middle of the street of the city. On either side of the river is the tree of life with its twelve kinds of fruit, producing its fruit each month; and the leaves of the tree are for the healing of the nations.
points.apply: Take one small step this week to care for your parish: serve, tidy, visit or give.

sub: The path of the righteous like the light of dawn.
The Way of Thomas kept for two thousand years.
I am the way.
q: But the path of the righteous is like the light of dawn, which shines brighter and brighter until full day.
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
points.apply: Teach a child one prayer of our tradition this week.

sub: From the beginning it was not so.
It is to peace that God has called you.
The household as the first church.
q: Therefore a man leaves his father and his mother and clings to his wife, and they become one flesh.
So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore what God has joined together, let no one separate.
points.apply: Pray with your spouse or family tonight for peace in your home.

concl: Thomas asked, went and confessed: “My Lord and my God!” Through him, according to tradition, the Gospel reached our land, and the Church is built on the foundation of the apostles.
We keep hold of the instruction we received, we guard the garden, and we hand on the faith to those who have not seen.
2027-07-03.resolve: This week, say Thomas's prayer at the elevation, thank one person who handed on the faith to you, and pray with your family for peace in the home.

intro: Theme: “For all who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.”
On the First Sunday of Kaitha, the Feast of the Twelve Apostles: twelve stones and one altar, the open prison door, the one Christ who is not divided, and the lowest place at the banquet.

sub: The Twelve chosen after a night of prayer.
Elijah's altar of twelve stones.
The fire from heaven.
q: When all the people saw it, they fell on their faces and said, “The Lord indeed is God; the Lord indeed is God.”
And when day came, he called his disciples and chose twelve of them, whom he also named apostles
points.apply: Learn the names of the Twelve and say them with your family this week.

points.h: Go, and tell the whole message
sub: Signs and wonders through the apostles.
Peter's shadow and the harvest of believers.
The open prison door.
q: May those who sow in tears reap with shouts of joy.
“Go, stand in the temple and tell the people the whole message about this life.”
points.apply: Say one honest word about your faith this week to someone who does not expect it.

sub: I belong to Paul, to Apollos, to Cephas.
One Lord, one faith, one baptism.
Unity in the parish and among the Churches.
q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized in the name of Paul?
points.apply: Make peace this week with one person in your family or parish with whom you are divided.

sub: Not the places of honour.
The apostles who argued and learned.
Invite the poor, who cannot repay.
q: Do not put yourself forward in the king’s presence or stand in the place of the great; for it is better to be told, “Come up here,” than to be put lower in the presence of a noble.
For all who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted.
points.apply: At the next gathering, take the last seat and serve another first.

concl: The Church is built on the Twelve, like Elijah's altar on twelve stones, and she is sent to tell the whole message.
Christ is not divided; let us be one in mind and purpose, take the lowest place, and invite those who cannot repay us.
2027-07-04.resolve: This week, name the Twelve in your prayers, make peace with someone, and take the last seat at the next meal.

intro: Theme: “This son of mine was dead and is alive again; he was lost and is found!”
On the Second Sunday of Kaitha: the love that chooses before it commands, the canopy over Zion, the Spirit who gives life, and the Father who runs to the younger son and goes out to the elder.

sub: Love before law.
The question of Moses.
Well-being for you and your descendants.
q: And because he loved your ancestors, he chose their descendants after them.
For God so loved the world that he gave his only Son, so that everyone who believes in him may not perish but may have eternal life.
points.apply: Thank God this week for one way he loved your family before you were born.

points.h: A canopy against the heat and the storm
sub: The Branch of the Lord.
Cloud by day and fire by night.
Shelter in the monsoon.
q: It will serve as a pavilion, a shade by day from the heat, and a refuge and a shelter from the storm and rain.
See, the home of God is among mortals. He will dwell with them; they will be his peoples, and God himself will be with them;
points.apply: Be a shelter this week for one person in your parish who is in a storm.

sub: Competence from God.
A covenant of the Spirit.
Boldness without pride.
q: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
who has made us competent to be ministers of a new covenant, not of letter but of spirit; for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life.
points.apply: Read a page of the Gospel each day and ask the Spirit to write it on your heart.

sub: The younger son comes to himself.
Robe, ring and feast.
The elder son and the open door.
q: As a father has compassion for his children, so the Lord has compassion for those who fear him.
But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion; he ran and put his arms around him and kissed him.
points.apply: Go to confession, or go out to someone who is angry at mercy.

concl: God chooses because he loves, shelters his people like a canopy, writes his law on their hearts, and runs to meet the one who returns.
Let us go home, and let us open the door to our brothers and sisters.
2027-07-11.resolve: This week, return to the Father, welcome someone home, and pray for those who are still far away.

intro: Theme: “Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven.”
Trials that teach endurance, faith that forgives, and the plain confession of a mother and her three-year-old son.

sub: Joy that knows nothing is wasted.
Ask God, who gives generously.
Faith that does not doubt.
q: For the Lord gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding;
My brothers and sisters, whenever you face trials of any kind, consider it nothing but joy, because you know that the testing of your faith produces endurance;
points.apply: Ask for wisdom each morning this week about one decision.

sub: Leaves without fruit.
The mountain and the faith that moves it.
The grudge that blocks the prayer.
q: If you do not stand firm in faith, you shall not stand at all.
So I tell you, whatever you ask for in prayer, believe that you have received it, and it will be yours.
points.apply: Forgive one person before your next prayer.

sub: “But if not.”
Stephen's face like an angel's.
The Spirit speaks in the hour of trial.
q: If our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the furnace of blazing fire and out of your hand, O king, let him deliver us.
Everyone therefore who acknowledges me before others, I also will acknowledge before my Father in heaven;
points.apply: Answer one question about your faith this week simply, kindly and without fear.

concl: Trials teach endurance, faith asks and forgives, and the Spirit speaks in the hour of witness.
A mother and a child at Tarsus show that nobody is too small to confess Christ.
2027-07-15.resolve: This week, ask God for wisdom each morning, forgive before you pray, and speak plainly and kindly about your faith.

intro: Theme: “As long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world.”
On the Third Sunday of Kaitha: the God who saves before he commands, the vineyard that must bear fruit, the grief that turns us back, and the sight that ends in worship.

points.h: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out
sub: Grace before law.
The Ten Words and the Lord's Day.
Honour your father and your mother.
q: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery;
“If you love me, you will keep my commandments.
points.apply: Keep this Sunday as a true day of rest and of the Lord, with your family.

points.h: What more was there to do for my vineyard?
sub: The work of the beloved.
Wild grapes instead of grapes.
Justice and righteousness as fruit.
q: he expected justice, but saw bloodshed; righteousness, but heard a cry!
I am the vine, you are the branches. Those who abide in me and I in them bear much fruit, because apart from me you can do nothing.
points.apply: Name one fruit of justice or mercy that you will give this month.

sub: Worldly grief and godly grief.
Judas and Peter.
The fruits of repentance.
q: rend your hearts and not your clothing. Return to the Lord, your God, for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love,
For godly grief produces a repentance that leads to salvation and brings no regret, but worldly grief produces death.
points.apply: Make a good confession this month, and repair one wrong.

sub: The man born blind: mud, Siloam, the Sent One.
Sight grows into faith.
Jesus goes looking for the one who was driven out.
q: the Lord opens the eyes of the blind.
He said, “Lord, I believe.” And he worshiped him.
points.apply: Each day this week, ask the Lord to open your eyes to one person or one need you have not seen.

concl: The God who saves gives the law, tends the vineyard, turns us back with godly grief and opens our eyes.
Let us keep his day, bear his fruit, repent with our whole heart and say, “Lord, I believe.”
2027-07-18.resolve: This week, keep the Lord's Day, repair one wrong, and ask the Lord to open your eyes to someone you have not seen.

intro: Theme: “You abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition.”
On the Fourth Sunday of Kaitha: the voice of God from the fire, Corban and the care of parents, and boasting only in the Lord.

points.h: The voice of God out of the fire
sub: The Ten Words are spoken for life.
The fourth commandment opens the table of love.
Today we have seen that God may speak and a person may live.
q: Honor your father and your mother, as the Lord your God commanded you, so that your days may be long and that it may go well with you in the land that the Lord your God is giving you.
for indeed our God is a consuming fire.
points.apply: Honour a parent or elder this week with one concrete act: a visit, a call, a meal together.

sub: Heart far from God, lips near.
A gift cannot replace the care of a father or mother.
Tradition must serve the word of God.
q: The Lord said: Because these people draw near with their mouths and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me, and their worship of me is a human commandment learned by rote;
You abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition.
points.apply: Ask whether any gift or custom of yours is a way of escaping a plain duty at home.

points.h: The fire that devours, and the one who boasts
sub: Manasseh devoured Ephraim.
Compare yourself with the Lord, not with others.
The Lord commends the humble.
q: Manasseh devoured Ephraim, and Ephraim Manasseh, and together they were against Judah. For all this his anger has not turned away; his hand is stretched out still.
“Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord.”
points.apply: Make one move this week toward peace with a relative with whom you are not speaking.

concl: God's commandments are his own voice, spoken for life, and they begin with honouring those who gave us life.
Let no tradition, gift or pride make the word of God void in us: let us boast only in the Lord.
2027-07-25.resolve: This week, honour a parent or an elder in a concrete way, seek peace in the family, and keep the heart clean before the Lord.

intro: Theme: “For it is the God who said, ‘Let light shine out of darkness,’ who has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.”
The preacher with nothing to hide, the light that has a face, and the Yes that needs no oath.

sub: God's mercy in the ministry.
No cunning, no falsifying of the word.
The open statement of the truth.
q: The Lord said: Because these people draw near with their mouths and honor me with their lips, while their hearts are far from me
But we have this treasure in clay jars, so that it may be made clear that this extraordinary power belongs to God and does not come from us.
points.apply: Tell one person this week, simply and honestly, what you believe and why.

sub: Light out of darkness.
We proclaim Christ, not ourselves.
The image of God.
q: Then God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.
He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation;
points.apply: Spend five minutes this week looking at a crucifix or an image of Christ and thanking God for his face.

sub: Locking people out of the kingdom.
Zeal without conversion.
A Church that is a door.
q: Ah, you who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness for light and light for darkness
“But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you lock people out of the kingdom of heaven. For you do not go in yourselves, and when others are going in, you stop them.
points.apply: Welcome someone who is new, shy or distant in your parish this week.

sub: The altar makes the gift sacred.
God hears every word.
Yes, Yes and No, No.
q: You shall not make wrongful use of the name of the Lord your God, for the Lord will not acquit anyone who misuses his name.
Let your word be ‘Yes, Yes’ or ‘No, No’; anything more than this comes from the evil one.
points.apply: Keep one delayed promise before the week ends.

concl: Paul states the truth openly and proclaims Christ and not himself; Jesus warns the gatekeepers who play with words.
Let our word be true, and let the light of Christ's face shine through it.
2027-07-01.resolve: This week, keep one delayed promise, welcome one person at the door of the parish, and pray before you speak.

intro: Theme: “Whoever welcomes you welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.”
The Seventy sent in pairs, the rivers in the wilderness, the love from which nothing can separate us, and the cost and the reward of discipleship.

sub: Seventy others, sent in pairs.
The mission of every baptised person.
Addai and Mari among the Seventy, by tradition.
q: But Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the Lord ’s people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit on them!”
The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; therefore ask the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.
points.apply: Pray for labourers each day this week, by name.

sub: God answers the poor and thirsty.
Do not fear, I am with you.
The Gospel opens springs.
q: I will open rivers on the bare heights, and fountains in the midst of the valleys; I will make the wilderness a pool of water, and the dry land springs of water.
On the last day of the festival, the great day, while Jesus was standing there, he cried out, “Let anyone who is thirsty come to me, and let the one who believes in me drink.
points.apply: Bring one dry place in your family or parish to the Lord in prayer this week.

sub: God is for us.
More than conquerors.
The open heart of the First Friday.
q: do not fear, for I am with you, do not be afraid, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my victorious right hand.
If God is for us, who is against us?
points.apply: Name one fear to the Lord on this First Friday and hand it over to him.

sub: Christ before everything.
Take up the cross.
Welcome in his name.
q: If your enemies are hungry, give them bread to eat; and if they are thirsty, give them water to drink
And whoever gives even a cup of cold water to one of these little ones in the name of a disciple, truly I tell you, none of these will lose their reward.
points.apply: Welcome one person this week with a glass of water and a few minutes of your time.

concl: The Seventy were ordinary disciples, sent in pairs with peace on their lips, and the mission belongs to all the baptised.
Nothing can separate us from the love of Christ; let us love him first and welcome others in his name.
2027-07-02.resolve: This week, pray for labourers, bring one fear to the open heart of Jesus, and welcome one person with a cup of cold water.

intro: Theme: “Son, go and work in the vineyard today.”
The divided table at Corinth, the Lord's Supper in its first written form, and the son who said No and went.

sub: Rich and poor at one table.
Paul's anger as love for the poor.
Not really the Lord's supper.
q: Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house; when you see the naked, to cover them, and not to hide yourself from your own kin?
Because there is one bread, we who are many are one body, for we all partake of the one bread.
points.apply: Greet or invite one person in your parish whom you usually do not notice.

points.h: This is my body for you
sub: The oldest account of the Eucharist.
Do this in remembrance of me.
Discerning the body.
q: This day shall be a day of remembrance for you. You shall celebrate it as a festival to the Lord ; throughout your generations you shall observe it as a perpetual ordinance.
For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord’s death until he comes.
points.apply: Prepare for the next Qurbana: make peace, and pray before the Blessed Sacrament for a few minutes.

points.h: Which of the two did the will of his father?
sub: A No that becomes a Yes.
A Yes that is only words.
Change of mind and heart.
q: rend your hearts and not your clothing. Return to the Lord , your God, for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love, and relents from punishing.
Not everyone who says to me, ‘Lord, Lord,’ will enter the kingdom of heaven, but only the one who does the will of my Father in heaven.
points.apply: Name one No you have given to God, and take one step back toward him today.

sub: The vineyard in the monsoon.
Kaitha, the season of fruit.
Yes with the hands.
q: I delight to do your will, O my God; your law is within my heart.
points.apply: Do today the one task you have been calling Later.

concl: The Lord's table is one table and one body; to eat the one bread and to despise the poor is a contradiction.
The Father asks for a Yes that works: let us go and work in the vineyard today.
2027-07-05.resolve: This week, make peace before the Qurbana, share with someone in need, and do the task you have delayed.

intro: Theme: “Be infants in evil, but in thinking be adults.”
A worship where the stranger says “God is really among you”, the gift that is traded and not buried, and the child who chose well and forgave.

points.h: Infants in evil, adults in thinking
sub: Innocence and wisdom together.
Gifts of the Spirit for building up.
Worship the stranger can understand.
q: Whatever your hand finds to do, do with your might
Brothers and sisters, do not be children in your thinking; rather, be infants in evil, but in thinking be adults.
points.apply: Look at your parish's worship with the eyes of a visitor and do one thing to make it welcoming.

points.h: Do business until I come back
sub: Each servant given a pound.
The two who traded.
Faithful in a very little.
q: A slack hand causes poverty, but the hand of the diligent makes rich.
Whoever is faithful in a very little is faithful also in much; and whoever is dishonest in a very little is dishonest also in much.
points.apply: Name one gift and use it for others before the end of the month.

sub: “You are a harsh man.”
Fear that buries the gift.
The generous giver.
q: Let the favor of the Lord our God be upon us, and prosper for us the work of our hands
From everyone to whom much has been given, much will be required; and from the one to whom much has been entrusted, even more will be demanded.
points.apply: Say a short prayer today: “Lord, you are good; help me trust you and use what you have given.”

sub: Saint Maria Goretti: a child in age, clear in choice.
Forgiving the one who hurt her.
Pure in heart.
q: Blessed are the pure in heart, for they will see God.
Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.
points.apply: Pray for someone who has hurt you, and forgive one small thing today.

concl: Be innocent about evil and wise in judgement; let worship be so true that the stranger says, “God is really among you.”
The Lord has entrusted gifts to each of us; let us trade with them in trust until he comes, and overcome evil with good.
2027-07-06.resolve: This week, make one gift of yours useful to others, welcome a visitor at the Qurbana, and pray for someone who has hurt you.

intro: Theme: “My sheep hear my voice. I know them, and they follow me.”
The man of God who pursues righteousness, the good confession made before many witnesses, and the voice of the Shepherd that no one can silence.

sub: Shun the love of money.
Six quiet virtues.
The good fight of the faith.
q: Whoever pursues righteousness and kindness will find life and honor.
But as for you, man of God, shun all this; pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, endurance, gentleness.
points.apply: Practise one of the six virtues with one particular person this week.

sub: Many witnesses.
Christ before Pilate.
Keep the commandment without spot or blame.
q: I will also speak of your decrees before kings, and shall not be put to shame.
Fight the good fight of the faith; take hold of the eternal life, to which you were called and for which you made the good confession in the presence of many witnesses.
points.apply: Say one word of faith, kindly and clearly, where it is usually kept silent.

sub: Hear, be known, follow.
The works testify.
No one will snatch them from his hand.
q: Know that the Lord is God. It is he that made us, and we are his; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.
My sheep hear my voice. I know them, and they follow me.
points.apply: Read the Gospel of the day each morning before looking at the phone.

concl: Faith is a fight fought with quiet virtues, and a confession made by a life.
The Shepherd knows his sheep, and no one can snatch them from his hand.
2027-07-07.resolve: This week, practise one virtue, read the Gospel each morning, and follow his voice.

intro: Theme: “Very truly, I tell you, before Abraham was, I am.”
Prayer with the spirit and with the mind, the Amen that builds up the Church, and the Lord who is before Abraham.

points.h: Pray with the spirit and with the mind
sub: The gift of tongues and its limit.
Heart and head together.
Sing praise with understanding.
q: For God is the king of all the earth; sing praises with a psalm.
What should I do then? I will pray with the spirit, but I will pray with the mind also; I will sing praise with the spirit, but I will sing praise with the mind also.
points.apply: Follow every prayer of the next Qurbana in your own language.

sub: Thanksgiving that all can answer.
Five words with the mind.
The growth of the Church.
q: Then Ezra blessed the Lord, the great God, and all the people answered, “Amen, Amen,” lifting up their hands.
Nevertheless, in church I would rather speak five words with my mind, in order to instruct others also, than ten thousand words in a tongue.
points.apply: Say each Amen at the Qurbana as a word you mean.

sub: Abraham rejoiced to see his day.
The name spoken at the bush.
The Lord who is with us.
q: God said to Moses, “I am who I am.”
Jesus said to them, “Very truly, I tell you, before Abraham was, I am.”
points.apply: Keep one saying of Jesus this week in one concrete action.

concl: Prayer is of the Spirit and of the mind, and the Amen of the people builds up the Church.
The One who is before Abraham is with us at every Qurbana.
2027-07-08.resolve: This week, pray with understanding, say your Amen with a whole heart, and keep his word.

intro: Theme: “Do not fear, for I am with you.”
The saint of the frontier city, the name of Jesus that is no charm, the weapons that build up, and the sparrows that are counted.

points.h: Do not fear, for I am with you
sub: The promise to Jacob.
The small and the weak.
God's victorious right hand.
q: Do not fear, you worm Jacob, you insect Israel! I will help you, says the Lord; your Redeemer is the Holy One of Israel.
Are not five sparrows sold for two pennies? Yet not one of them is forgotten in God’s sight.
points.apply: Give one particular fear to the Lord each evening this week.

points.h: Not a charm, but the name
sub: The sons of Sceva.
The burning of the books.
Trust in Christ alone.
q: Some take pride in chariots, and some in horses, but our pride is in the name of the Lord our God.
A number of those who practiced magic collected their books and burned them publicly; when the value of these books was calculated, it was found to come to fifty thousand silver coins.
points.apply: Put away any amulet or horoscope you trust.

sub: The weapons of our warfare.
For building up, not for tearing down.
The teacher as Mar Yakob was.
q: The Lord is my strength and my shield; in him my heart trusts; so I am helped, and my heart exults, and with my song I give thanks to him.
Indeed, we live as human beings, but we do not wage war according to human standards; for the weapons of our warfare are not merely human, but they have divine power to destroy strongholds.
points.apply: Teach one prayer to one child this week.

sub: Acknowledge him.
The Holy Spirit will teach you.
Counted and held.
q: Now go, and I will be with your mouth and teach you what you are to speak.
for the Holy Spirit will teach you at that very hour what you ought to say.
points.apply: Acknowledge your faith once, quietly and with respect, where it is usually left unsaid.

concl: God holds the small and the afraid with his right hand, and he does not forget one sparrow.
Let us trust in the name of Jesus alone and bear witness without fear.
2027-07-09.resolve: This week, give one fear to the Lord, put away one false trust, and say one word of faith.

intro: Theme: “When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, ‘Son, your sins are forgiven.’”
We are the temple of the living God; four friends and a hole in the roof; and the Son of Man who has authority to forgive.

points.h: The temple of the living God
sub: Not mismatched.
God lives in us and walks among us.
A place that belongs to God.
q: And I will walk among you, and will be your God, and you shall be my people.
What agreement has the temple of God with idols? For we are the temple of the living God; as God said, “I will live in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.”
points.apply: Treat your body and your home as his dwelling this week.

points.h: Come out from sin, and welcome your neighbour
sub: Not from people, but from idols and impurity.
Respect for neighbours of every faith.
A Father who welcomes.
q: Depart, depart, go out from there! Touch no unclean thing; go out from the midst of it, purify yourselves, you who carry the vessels of the Lord.
Therefore come out from them, and be separate from them, says the Lord, and touch nothing unclean; then I will welcome you.
points.apply: Step out of one dishonest partnership.

sub: Four friends.
The hole in the roof.
Faith that carries another.
q: who forgives all your iniquity, who heals all your diseases,
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
points.apply: Carry one named person to Jesus by prayer and a visit.

sub: Only God forgives.
The visible sign of the invisible gift.
The sacrament of mercy.
q: I, I am He who blots out your transgressions for my own sake, and I will not remember your sins.
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins
points.apply: Plan your next confession.

concl: God dwells in us as in a temple, and he forgives in the person of his Son.
Let us be the four friends who carry others to him.
2027-07-10.resolve: This week, carry one person to Jesus, step out of one false yoke, and go to confession.

intro: Theme: “Everyone then who hears these words of mine and acts on them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock.”
Trial and temptation, the two births, the Father of lights and his first fruits, and the house on the rock.

points.h: Blessed is the one who endures
sub: Trial and temptation.
God tests, never tempts.
The crown of life.
q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither.
Blessed is anyone who endures temptation. Such a one has stood the test and will receive the crown of life that the Lord has promised to those who love him.
points.apply: Stop one growing desire at its first thought, with a short prayer.

sub: Desire, sin, death.
The word of truth.
First fruits of his creatures.
q: The Lord will give what is good, and our land will yield its increase.
In fulfillment of his own purpose he gave us birth by the word of truth, so that we would become a kind of first fruits of his creatures.
points.apply: Each night this week thank the Father for three gifts.

sub: Not those who say Lord, Lord.
The floods and the winds.
Hearing and acting.
q: The Lord is my rock, my fortress, and my deliverer, my God, my rock in whom I take refuge.
Everyone then who hears these words of mine and acts on them will be like a wise man who built his house on rock.
points.apply: Act on one word of Jesus this week in a concrete deed.

concl: The Father of lights gives us birth by his word and tests us in order to strengthen us, and never tempts us.
The wise build on the rock by doing what he says.
2027-07-12.resolve: This week, cut one temptation early, count three gifts each night, and do one word of the Lord.

intro: Theme: “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.”
The war within that becomes war without, the grace that God gives to the humble, and the kingdom that already belongs to the poor.

points.h: Where do our quarrels come from?
sub: Cravings at war within us.
Envy and the road of Cain.
Prayer that only wants more.
q: The Lord said to Cain, “Why are you angry, and why has your countenance fallen? If you do well, will you not be accepted? And if you do not do well, sin is lurking at the door; its desire is for you, but you must master it.”
Those conflicts and disputes among you, where do they come from? Do they not come from your cravings that are at war within you?
points.apply: Name the craving behind one quarrel you carry, and hand it to God in prayer.

points.h: God gives grace to the humble
sub: The jealous love of God.
Friend of the world, enemy of God.
Submit, resist, and the devil will flee.
q: Toward the scorners he is scornful, but to the humble he shows favor.
Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
points.apply: Bend your pride this week in one small matter: say sorry first.

sub: The kingdom is theirs now.
Hunger and tears will be reversed.
Woe to the comfortable and the praised.
q: But the meek shall inherit the land, and delight themselves in abundant prosperity.
“Woe to you when all speak well of you, for that is what their ancestors did to the false prophets.
points.apply: Share food, money or time with one person who has less than you.

concl: Our quarrels begin in our cravings; grace begins in humility and the kingdom begins with the poor.
Let us make peace first, and let us be glad to be citizens of a kingdom that cannot be bought.
2027-07-13.resolve: This week, make the first move toward peace with one person, ask God for what you truly need, and share with someone who has less.

intro: Theme: “Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.”
The courage of faith in the face of wasting and loss, the house that God prepares, and the Lord who is the grain that falls into the earth.

points.h: So we do not lose heart
sub: The One who raised Jesus will raise us.
Treasure in clay jars.
Suffering offered for others becomes thanksgiving.
q: May those who sow in tears reap with shouts of joy.
So we do not lose heart. Even though our outer nature is wasting away, our inner nature is being renewed day by day.
points.apply: Place one discouragement of this week in the hands of the risen Lord each morning.

points.h: Look at what cannot be seen
sub: A slight momentary affliction.
An eternal weight of glory.
The earthly tent and the house from God.
q: I consider that the sufferings of this present time are not worth comparing with the glory about to be revealed to us.
For we know that if the earthly tent we live in is destroyed, we have a building from God, a house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.
points.apply: Pray for your dead and for the sick in your parish, and visit one of them.

sub: The hour has come: the Cross is the glory.
Whoever serves me must follow me.
The voice: I will glorify it again.
q: Fool! What you sow does not come to life unless it dies.
Whoever serves me must follow me, and where I am, there will my servant be also. Whoever serves me, the Father will honor.
points.apply: Choose one small dying to self this week, and do it quietly.

concl: The One who raised Jesus will raise us; our inner nature is renewed, and the house from God is prepared.
So let us be willing to fall like the grain, for the harvest is the Lord's.
2027-07-14.resolve: This week, offer one trouble to the risen Lord each morning, pray for the sick and the dead, and let one small seed of yourself fall for someone else.

intro: Theme: “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it!”
The prayer that holds on until the little cloud appears, the Mother who heard the word and kept it, the God of all consolation, and the Gospel that came from Edessa to the East.

sub: The drought and the mountain.
Six times nothing; the seventh, a little cloud.
A human being like us.
q: Then he said, “Go again seven times.” At the seventh time he said, “Look, a little cloud no bigger than a person’s hand is rising out of the sea.”
Elijah was a human being like us, and he prayed fervently that it might not rain, and for three years and six months it did not rain on the earth.
points.apply: Bring one old prayer back to God each day this week.

points.h: Mary hears the word and keeps it
sub: The swept house must be filled.
Blessed rather are those who hear and obey.
The scapular as a sign of belonging.
q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
But he said, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it!”
points.apply: Choose one line of the Sunday Gospel and live it through the week.

sub: Consolation received is consolation shared.
Mary at the Cross, Comforter of the Afflicted.
Sitting with the grieving.
q: As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you; you shall be comforted in Jerusalem.
Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation,
points.apply: Visit or call one person who is grieving or afflicted.

points.h: Mar Mari and the word that does not return empty
sub: Disciple of Mar Addai, missionary of the East.
The Anaphora of Addai and Mari.
From Edessa to the Tigris, by the word.
q: so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.
And how are they to hear without someone to proclaim him?
points.apply: Thank God for the faith handed on to you, and pass one word of it to someone this week.

concl: A little cloud, a listening Mother, a God who consoles and a word that does not return empty: so the rain of the Gospel has watered the world.
Let us pray again, hear the word and keep it, and comfort one another.
2027-07-16.resolve: This week, bring one old prayer to God again each day, keep one line of the Gospel, and console one person.

intro: Theme: “Sir, what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.”
No favouritism in the assembly, the God who chose the poor, and the great dinner to which everyone is invited.

sub: Gold rings and dirty clothes.
The royal law of love.
One place where no one is ranked by his wallet.
q: You shall not render an unjust judgment; you shall not be partial to the poor or defer to the great: with justice you shall judge your neighbor.
My brothers and sisters, do you with your acts of favoritism really believe in our glorious Lord Jesus Christ?
points.apply: Greet and sit beside someone whom nobody sits with at the next parish gathering.

sub: Rich in faith, heirs of the kingdom.
The preferential love of the Church.
What the poor teach us about faith.
q: He raises the poor from the dust, and lifts the needy from the ash heap, to make them sit with princes, with the princes of his people.
Has not God chosen the poor in the world to be rich in faith and to be heirs of the kingdom that he has promised to those who love him?
points.apply: Share some of your time or means with one poor family or person this week.

sub: Land, oxen and marriage.
Good things before the call.
Polite excuses.
q: On this mountain the Lord of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of rich food, a feast of well-aged wines, of rich food filled with marrow, of well-aged wines strained clear.
At the time for the dinner he sent his slave to say to those who had been invited, ‘Come; for everything is ready now.’
points.apply: Name your usual excuse and set aside one hour this week for God.

sub: The streets and lanes.
The host's urgent love.
The house must be filled.
q: The rich and the poor have this in common: the Lord is the maker of them all.
And the slave said, “Sir, what you ordered has been done, and there is still room.”
points.apply: Invite someone who cannot invite you back to your table or your church.

concl: The Church's table is the Lord's table: no favourites, a place for the poor, and room for one more.
Let us answer the call without excuse and make room for those who have not been asked.
2027-07-17.resolve: This week, greet someone nobody sits with, invite someone who cannot repay you, and set aside an hour to answer God's call.

intro: Theme: “For just as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is also dead.”
A faith brought to completion by obedience, a stranger's open door, and the Lord who would gather us under his wings.

sub: Abraham believed first.
The mountain of Moriah made his faith visible.
Faith is a gift; a gift is meant to be used.
q: And he believed the Lord; and the Lord reckoned it to him as righteousness.
You see that faith was active along with his works, and faith was brought to completion by the works.
points.apply: Choose one act this week through which your faith will be seen.

sub: A stranger who believed.
She risked her life and her house.
The least and the greatest justified alike.
q: But Rahab the prostitute, with her family and all who belonged to her, Joshua spared. Her family has lived in Israel ever since. For she hid the messengers whom Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.
By faith Rahab the prostitute did not perish with those who were disobedient, because she had received the spies in peace.
points.apply: Open your door, your table or your time to one person who is a stranger to you.

sub: The grief of Jesus over Jerusalem.
God's love never forces.
Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.
q: he will cover you with his pinions, and under his wings you will find refuge; his faithfulness is a shield and buckler.
How often have I desired to gather your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings, and you were not willing!
points.apply: Each evening this week, ask the Lord to gather you and the people you love under his wings.

concl: Faith is a gift of God, and it is alive when it opens the hand and the door.
The Lord is always the one who gathers; our part is to be willing.
2027-07-19.resolve: This week, do one act that shows your faith, open a door to a stranger, and run to the Lord's wings each evening.

intro: Theme: “And a harvest of righteousness is sown in peace for those who make peace.”
Two wisdoms, the harvest of envy and the harvest of peace, and a prophet who was not accepted at home.

sub: Wisdom shown in a good life.
Earthly wisdom: envy and ambition.
Wisdom from above: pure, peaceable, merciful.
q: Her ways are ways of pleasantness, and all her paths are peace.
But the wisdom from above is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, willing to yield, full of mercy and good fruits, without a trace of partiality or hypocrisy.
points.apply: Choose one mark of the wisdom from above and ask for it each morning this week.

sub: Where envy rules, disorder follows.
The envious are never at rest.
Rejoice with those who rejoice.
q: but for Cain and his offering he had no regard. So Cain was very angry, and his countenance fell.
For where there is envy and selfish ambition, there will also be disorder and wickedness of every kind.
points.apply: Thank God aloud this week for a good that has come to someone you envy.

sub: Is not this Joseph's son?
God's mercy goes beyond every border.
The first rejection; his hour had not yet come.
q: “Go now to Zarephath, which belongs to Sidon, and live there; for I have commanded a widow there to feed you.”
Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in the prophet’s hometown.
points.apply: Listen this week with fresh attention to someone you take for granted.

concl: The wisdom from above is known by its fruit: purity, peace, gentleness and mercy.
Envy and familiarity close our eyes; peace opens them to see what God is doing.
2027-07-20.resolve: This week, rejoice with someone you envy, make peace where you can, and see Christ in the people you know best.

intro: Theme: “So if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: everything old has passed away; see, everything has become new!”
The new creation, God's appeal through his ambassadors, and the call of the fishermen.

sub: Christ died for all.
No one is seen from a merely human point of view.
The font, the confession, the Qurbana: the old passes away.
q: I am about to do a new thing; now it springs forth, do you not perceive it? I will make a way in the wilderness and rivers in the desert.
So if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: everything old has passed away; see, everything has become new!
points.apply: Name one old thing in you that you ask God to make new this week.

sub: God made the first move.
God appeals through human voices.
The sinless one made sin for us.
q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news, who announces salvation, who says to Zion, “Your God reigns.”
So we are ambassadors for Christ, since God is making his appeal through us; we entreat you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God.
points.apply: Make the first move toward someone with whom you are at odds.

sub: Four fishermen, ordinary men.
They left their nets at once.
The apostolic Church begins.
q: He returned from following him, took the yoke of oxen, and slaughtered them; using the equipment from the oxen, he boiled their flesh, and gave it to the people, and they ate. Then he set out and followed Elijah, and became his servant.
And Jesus said to them, “Follow me and I will make you fish for people.” And immediately they left their nets and followed him.
points.apply: Name one net you are holding and take one step to let it go.

concl: In Christ everything has become new, and God entrusts to us the message of reconciliation.
The Lord who called the fishermen calls us, and our answer is to leave a net and go to the brother or sister.
2027-07-21.resolve: This week, make the first move toward peace, go to confession, and leave one net behind.

intro: Theme: “Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, ‘I have seen the Lord’.”
The love that is not separated, the name that is called, the mission “go to my brothers”, and the apostle of the apostles.

sub: At the cross, with the mother of Jesus.
At the tomb, in the dark.
Nothing in all creation can separate us.
q: Set me as a seal upon your heart, as a seal upon your arm; for love is strong as death, passion fierce as the grave.

For I am convinced that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor rulers, nor things present, nor things to come, nor powers, nor height, nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
points.apply: Stay near someone who is suffering this week.

sub: She seeks and weeps.
The Good Shepherd calls by name.
Known by the voice, not by the face.
q: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name, you are mine.
Jesus said to her, “Mary!” She turned and said to him in Hebrew, “Rabbouni!” (which means Teacher).
points.apply: Listen each morning for the Lord calling you by name.

points.h: Do not hold on, but go
sub: A new nearness through the Ascension.
“My brothers”: the Father is shared.
The mission is entrusted to a woman.
q: I will tell of your name to my brothers and sisters; in the midst of the congregation I will praise you:
Jesus said to her, “Do not hold on to me, because I have not yet ascended to the Father. But go to my brothers and say to them, ‘I am ascending to my Father and your Father, to my God and your God.’”
points.apply: Tell one person this week something good that the Lord has done for you.

sub: “I have seen the Lord.”
An idle tale to the Twelve.
The Church's witness begins with her voice.
q: I shall not die, but I shall live, and recount the deeds of the Lord.
Mary Magdalene went and announced to the disciples, “I have seen the Lord”; and she told them that he had said these things to her.
points.apply: Be a witness in your home this week: say aloud where you have seen the Lord.

concl: Saint Mary Magdalene stayed when others fled, heard her name, and was sent to tell the Twelve.
The Lord calls us by name and sends us to our brothers and sisters, to say what we have seen.
2027-07-22.resolve: This week, stay near one who suffers, listen for your name, and tell someone, “I have seen the Lord.”

intro: Theme: “and that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith, as you are being rooted and grounded in love.”
Christ in the heart, roots in love, the breadth and depth of his love, and the blind man healed in stages.

points.h: Christ in the heart, roots in love
sub: Paul kneels for every family.
Strength in the inner being.
Roots by the stream; a foundation in the flood.
q: They shall be like a tree planted by water, sending out its roots by the stream. It shall not fear when heat comes, and its leaves shall stay green; in the year of drought it is not anxious, and it does not cease to bear fruit.
and that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith, as you are being rooted and grounded in love.
points.apply: Kneel for your family each evening this week.

sub: The love of Christ that surpasses knowledge.
The shape of the Cross.
Filled with all the fullness of God.
q: Your steadfast love, O Lord, extends to the heavens, your faithfulness to the clouds.

I pray that you may have the power to comprehend, with all the saints, what is the breadth and length and height and depth, and to know the love of Christ that surpasses knowledge, so that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.
points.apply: Spend ten minutes before a crucifix this week and give thanks for his love.

sub: Friends bring the blind man.
“I can see people, but they look like trees, walking.”
The Lord touches again.
q: Open my eyes, so that I may behold wondrous things out of your law.
Then Jesus laid his hands on his eyes again; and he looked intently and his sight was restored, and he saw everything clearly.
points.apply: Bring someone who cannot yet see the way to Jesus by prayer and by a call or visit.

concl: Christ wants to live in our hearts, and his love has dimensions no mind can measure.
He is patient with our dim sight, and he touches us again until we see.
2027-07-23.resolve: This week, kneel for your family each evening, look long at the Cross, and bring one blind friend to Jesus.

intro: Theme: “Instead you ought to say, ‘If the Lord wishes, we will live and do this or that.’”
A life like a mist, a heart as wide as the Lord's, and a face set toward Jerusalem without fire from heaven.

sub: Plans made as if we owned tomorrow.
If the Lord wishes.
The good we know and do not do.
q: So teach us to count our days that we may gain a wise heart.
Yet you do not even know what tomorrow will bring. What is your life? For you are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.
points.apply: Offer one plan to the Lord this week, and do one good you have put off.

sub: “He does not follow with us.”
Moses and Eldad and Medad.
Good done in Christ's name is not to be forbidden.
q: But Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? Would that all the Lord’s people were prophets, and that the Lord would put his spirit on them!”
But Jesus said to him, “Do not stop him; for whoever is not against you is for you.”
points.apply: Thank God this week for a good work done by people outside your own group.

sub: The servant who sets his face like flint.
A village refuses; the sons of thunder want fire.
The Lamb rebukes them and moves on.
q: The Lord God helps me; therefore I have not been disgraced; therefore I have set my face like flint, and I know that I shall not be put to shame;
When the days drew near for him to be taken up, he set his face to go to Jerusalem.
points.apply: When someone refuses or hurts you this week, answer with patience and move on.

concl: Our lives are in the Lord's hands; we plan with humility and do the good we know.
His heart is wide, and his gentleness is the way of the Lamb on the road to the Cross.
2027-07-24.resolve: This week, say “If the Lord wishes” over every plan, do one good thing now, and bless the good that others do.

intro: Theme: “He raises up the poor from the dust; he lifts the needy from the ash heap.”
On the memorial of Saint Joachim and Saint Anne: the song of the barren, the faith of Abraham and Sarah, the chain of a family, and riches that must be given.

sub: Hannah's prayer and Mary's Magnificat.
Enlarge the tent: God turns shame into joy.
Joachim and Anne, according to tradition, prayed long for a child.
q: My heart exults in the Lord; my strength is exalted in my God.
Sing, O barren one who did not bear; burst into song and shout, you who have not been in labor!
points.apply: Pray the Magnificat this week for someone who is waiting for a child, a healing or a job.

points.h: By faith: a chain of generations
sub: Abraham and Sarah trusted the promise.
The genealogy: ordinary people who handed on the promise.
We are links in that chain.
q: By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to set out for a place that he was to receive as an inheritance; and he set out, not knowing where he was going.
An account of the genealogy of Jesus the Messiah, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
points.apply: Write down the names of your grandparents and thank God for what each handed on.

sub: Your riches have rotted: do not hoard.
The camel and the needle's eye.
Grace saves, and it asks for a giving heart.
q: Your riches have rotted, and your clothes are moth-eaten.
He replied, “What is impossible for mortals is possible for God.”
points.apply: Settle one debt or wage you owe, and give one gift to someone in need.

concl: Joachim and Anne, grandparents of Jesus, show how faith is handed on from one generation to the next, through prayer and patient trust.
What we cannot do, God can: let us trust, give and pass on the faith.
2027-07-26.resolve: This week, thank God for your grandparents by name, settle what you owe, and tell a young person how God has carried you.

intro: Theme: “You also must be patient. Strengthen your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is near.”
On the Fourth Tuesday of Kaitha: waiting like a farmer, enduring like Job, and keeping alert until the Son of Man comes.

sub: The early and the late rains.
Patience is strength of heart, not idleness.
No grumbling, no oaths: keep your word.
q: Let us know, let us press on to know the Lord; his appearing is as sure as the dawn; he will come to us like the showers, like the spring rains that water the earth.
Be patient, therefore, beloved, until the coming of the Lord. The farmer waits for the precious crop from the earth, being patient with it until it receives the early and the late rains.
points.apply: Spend one day this week without a single complaint about anyone.

sub: Blessed are those who endure.
Job lost everything and blessed the Lord.
The Lord is compassionate and merciful.
q: He said, “Naked I came from my mother’s womb, and naked shall I return there; the Lord gave, and the Lord has taken away; blessed be the name of the Lord.”
Indeed we call blessed those who showed endurance. You have heard of the endurance of Job, and you have seen the purpose of the Lord, how the Lord is compassionate and merciful.
points.apply: In a present trouble, say Job's words in your own prayer.

points.h: Keep alert: his words will not pass away
sub: The Son of Man will gather his elect from the ends of the earth.
Learn from the fig tree: small signs of summer.
Heaven and earth pass; the word remains.
q: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God will stand forever.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
points.apply: Each evening this week read one gospel verse and say: Come, Lord Jesus.

concl: We wait like the farmer: working, trusting, without grumbling, keeping our word.
The one who is coming has already come and is with us at the altar; his words will not pass away.
2027-07-27.resolve: This week, wait without complaining, keep every promise you make, and pray each evening: Come, Lord Jesus.

intro: Theme: “Unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.”
On the feast of Saint Alphonsa: a holy people as a sign, suffering offered with Christ, the grain that dies, and the harvest that needs laborers.

points.h: A holy people, a sign to the nations
sub: God establishes his people as holy.
The Lord opens the heavens and gives rain in its season.
Alphonsa's hidden life became a sign for Kerala and the world.
q: The Lord will establish you as his holy people, as he has sworn to you, if you keep the commandments of the Lord your God and walk in his ways.
But if it dies, it bears much fruit.
points.apply: Ask which small, hidden faithfulness of yours could be a sign to someone this week.

points.h: The Servant and suffering offered with Christ
sub: Christ's suffering alone has redeeming power.
He lets his friends share in it.
Offered in love, pain is never wasted.
q: The righteous one, my servant, shall make many righteous, and he shall bear their iniquities.
I am now rejoicing in my sufferings for your sake, and in my flesh I am completing what is lacking in Christ’s afflictions for the sake of his body, that is, the church.
points.apply: Offer one pain or inconvenience each day this week for a person you name.

points.h: Crucified with Christ: a grain that dies
sub: It is no longer I who live, but Christ.
Unless a grain falls and dies it remains a single grain.
Whoever serves me must follow me.
q: Out of his anguish he shall see light; he shall find satisfaction through his knowledge.
and it is no longer I who live, but it is Christ who lives in me.
points.apply: Do one hidden act of service this week without anyone knowing.

sub: The Lord looks at the crowds with compassion.
He asks us to pray for laborers.
Laborers can work even from a sickbed.
q: The Lord will open for you his rich storehouse, the heavens, to give the rain of your land in its season and to bless all your undertakings.
The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few;
points.apply: Visit one sick or lonely person this week, and pray for vocations.

concl: Saint Alphonsa shows that holiness is not noise but love hidden in ordinary days, and that suffering joined to Christ bears fruit.
The Lord of the harvest still sends laborers: let us offer ourselves.
2027-07-28.resolve: This week, offer one pain for a named person, visit someone who suffers, and do one hidden service.

intro: Theme: “I am the resurrection and the life… Do you believe this?”
On the memorial of Saint Martha: faith spoken in grief, love that serves, and drawing near to the Lord who kindles the fire.

sub: Grief and trust in the same breath.
The resurrection is a person standing before her.
A woman's confession: the Messiah, the Son of God.
q: Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Those who believe in me, even though they die, will live,
She said to him, “Yes, Lord, I believe that you are the Messiah, the Son of God, the one coming into the world.”
points.apply: Say aloud this week, in the middle of a worry, “Yes, Lord, I believe.”

sub: God loved us first.
Martha served at Bethany.
Welcoming a guest is welcoming Christ.
q: Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it.
Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God; everyone who loves is born of God and knows God.
points.apply: Welcome one guest, neighbour or stranger into your home or your day.

points.h: Draw near, and keep the fire
sub: Submit to God and draw near.
Humble yourselves before the Lord.
Jesus came to kindle fire on the earth.
q: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God will stand forever.
Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you.
points.apply: Give five silent minutes before the Lord each day this week, before your busiest hour.

concl: Martha shows that faith and service belong together, and that the Lord who loves our homes is the resurrection and the life.
Let us run to meet him, sit at his feet, and serve him in every guest.
2027-07-29.resolve: This week, welcome a guest, sit in silence five minutes a day, and say with Martha, “Yes, Lord, I believe.”

intro: Theme: “You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart… and your neighbor as yourself.”
On the Fourth Friday of Kaitha: boasting in the right place, the foundation that does not fade, and the one love of God and neighbour.

sub: The lowly are raised; the rich are brought low.
Wealth fades like the flower of the field.
Our worth is measured by God, not by possessions.
q: The grass withers, the flower fades, when the breath of the Lord blows upon it; surely the people are grass.
Let the believer who is lowly boast in being raised up,
points.apply: Hold loosely one thing you rely on, and share a part of it.

points.h: The foundation that does not fade
sub: The lawyer's question.
The Shema and Leviticus: the heart of Israel's law.
On these two hang all the law and the prophets.
q: You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your might.
On these two commandments hang all the law and the prophets.
points.apply: Say the Shema each morning: “Lord, I love you with all my heart.”

sub: No love of God without love of neighbour.
Love is the fulfilling of the law.
Shared wealth becomes a lasting treasure.
q: You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against any of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the Lord.
Love does no wrong to a neighbor; therefore, love is the fulfilling of the law.
points.apply: Do one concrete act of love for a neighbour you find hard.

concl: Everything that is gathered in our hands fades like grass; the love of God and neighbour is the one thing that stays.
The whole of Scripture hangs on it.
2027-07-30.resolve: This week, say the Shema each morning, share one possession, and love one hard neighbour in a concrete way.

intro: Theme: “Whatever you do, do everything for the glory of God.”
On the memorial of Saint Ignatius of Loyola: everything for the glory of God, counting the cost of discipleship, faith in prayer, and the love of truth.

points.h: Everything for the glory of God
sub: Eating, drinking, working, praying.
Find God in all things.
Give no offense, and seek the good of many.
q: The earth is the Lord’s and all that is in it,
So, whether you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do everything for the glory of God.
points.apply: Say each morning: “Lord, today everything for your glory.”

sub: Christ comes first, even before family.
The tower and the king.
Give up all that keeps you from him.
q: Prepare your work outside, get everything ready for you in the field; and after that build your house.
So therefore, none of you can become my disciple if you do not give up all your possessions.
points.apply: Write the cost and the gain of one decision you have postponed for Christ's sake.

points.h: Have faith, and love the truth
sub: Faith and prayer move mountains.
Deception is real; the defence is love of the truth.
Test everything; hold fast to what is good.
q: Then when you call upon me and come and pray to me, I will hear you.
but test everything; hold fast to what is good;
points.apply: Test one message you receive before you pass it on.

concl: Ignatius shows that a whole life can be given to the glory of God, in ordinary things, with a clear sense of the cost.
Let us offer everything and say: take, Lord, and receive.
2027-07-31.resolve: This week, offer your day each morning, count one cost honestly, and test what you read before you share it.
